objects.definition: struct IDSelector;
objects.description: Forward-declared selector interface used to restrict searches or removals to specific IDs. Only a forward declaration is present in this header; the full definition lives elsewhere (see impl/IDSelector.h).

objects.definition: struct RangeSearchResult;
objects.description: Forward-declared container to accumulate results of range_search queries. Only a forward declaration is present here; the full definition is provided elsewhere (see impl/AuxIndexStructures.h).

objects.definition: struct DistanceComputer;
objects.description: Forward-declared helper that computes distances for indexes supporting random access to stored vectors. Only a forward declaration is present here; implementation is elsewhere (see impl/DistanceComputer.h).

Base class for optional search parameters passed to Index::search and related methods. Currently provides an optional IDSelector to limit candidates. Subclasses may add fields; ownership remains with the caller. Destruction is virtual to enable dynamic_cast and safe polymorphic deletion.

Abstract base class for FAISS indexes that store and search vectors. Manages dimension, count, training state, and metric configuration. Provides the core virtual API: training, adding vectors (optionally with IDs), k-NN search, range search, reconstruction, residual computation, codec encode/decode, merging, and utilities. Some methods are pure virtual (add, search, reset), others have defaults that may throw if unsupported. Construction requires dimension and metric; destruction is virtual.

Enumeration of input numeric encodings supported by some Index methods that accept generic buffers: 32-bit float, 16-bit float, unsigned 8-bit, and signed 8-bit. Used with train_ex/add_ex/search_ex to select interpretation of the input pointer. Note: in this header only Float32 is accepted; others throw unless overridden by derived classes.

Exhaustive-search flat index that stores full float vectors uncompressed. Inherits IndexFlatCodes to manage raw code storage; supports L2 or inner-product metrics. Provides search, range search, reconstruction, encoding/decoding passthrough, and distance computation helpers. Construction requires dimensionality and metric; otherwise details like ownership and lifecycle follow faiss::Index semantics.

Flat index specialized for inner-product similarity. Thin subclass of IndexFlat that fixes the metric to METRIC_INNER_PRODUCT. Default constructor exists (likely for deserialization); main constructor takes dimensionality.

Flat index specialized for L2 distance. Adds an optional cache of precomputed L2 norms to accelerate distance computation via dot products. Provides methods to compute/clear the cache and overrides the distance computer to exploit it.

Flat index variant integrating Panorama storage/acceleration for L2. Maintains multi-level Panorama structure (n_levels, batch_size), cumulative sums, and enforces L2 metric. Overrides add/search/range_search/subset, reconstruction, removal, merge, and code ingestion to operate with the Panorama backend.
Convenience subclass of IndexFlatPanorama fixed to L2 metric. Constructor takes dimensionality, number of Panorama levels, and optional batch size.

Optimized flat index for 1D vectors (scalars). Maintains a permutation of database indices sorted by value. Optionally updates the permutation continuously on add; otherwise requires explicit update_permutation. Overrides add/reset/search; search returns L1 distances despite L2 base class.

Encapsulates the level-1 (coarse) quantizer used by IndexIVF. Holds the coarse quantizer Index, number of lists, training mode, ownership flag, optional clustering parameters and clustering index, plus helper methods for training and encoding/decoding list numbers. Construction/destruction ownership semantics depend on own_fields. Details of methods are defined elsewhere.

Search-time parameters for IVF indices. Controls nprobe, a cap on visited codes, optional nested parameters for the quantizer, and an opaque context passed to InvertedLists. Typedef alias IVFSearchParameters equals SearchParametersIVF.

Abstract scanner used by IVF searches to evaluate distances between a query and codes in a given inverted list, push results into heaps or range results. Holds query/list state, selection filter, and flags controlling heap behavior and label storage.

objects.definition:
struct IndexIVFInterface : Level1Quantizer {
    size_t nprobe = 1;    ///< number of probes at query time
    size_t max_codes = 0; ///< max nb of codes to visit to do a query

    explicit IndexIVFInterface(Index* quantizer = nullptr, size_t nlist = 0)
            : Level1Quantizer(quantizer, nlist) {}

    /** search a set of vectors, that are pre-quantized by the IVF
     *  quantizer. Fill in the corresponding heaps with the query
     *  results. The default implementation uses InvertedListScanners
     *  to do the search.
     *
     * @param n      nb of vectors to query
     * @param x      query vectors, size nx * d
     * @param assign coarse quantization indices, size nx * nprobe
     * @param centroid_dis
     *               distances to coarse centroids, size nx * nprobe
     * @param distance
     *               output distances, size n * k
     * @param labels output labels, size n * k
     * @param store_pairs store inv list index + inv list offset
     *                     instead in upper/lower 32 bit of result,
     *                     instead of ids (used for reranking).
     * @param params used to override the object's search parameters
     * @param stats  search stats to be updated (can be null)
     */
    virtual void search_preassigned(
            idx_t n,
            const float* x,
            idx_t k,
            const idx_t* assign,
            const float* centroid_dis,
            float* distances,
            idx_t* labels,
            bool store_pairs,
            const IVFSearchParameters* params = nullptr,
            IndexIVFStats* stats = nullptr) const = 0;

    /** Range search a set of vectors, that are pre-quantized by the IVF
     *  quantizer. Fill in the RangeSearchResults results. The default
     * implementation uses InvertedListScanners to do the search.
     *
     * @param n      nb of vectors to query
     * @param x      query vectors, size nx * d
     * @param assign coarse quantization indices, size nx * nprobe
     * @param centroid_dis
     *               distances to coarse centroids, size nx * nprobe
     * @param result Output results
     * @param store_pairs store inv list index + inv list offset
     *                     instead in upper/lower 32 bit of result,
     *                     instead of ids (used for reranking).
     * @param params used to override the object's search parameters
     * @param stats  search stats to be updated (can be null)
     */
    virtual void range_search_preassigned(
            idx_t nx,
            const float* x,
            float radius,
            const idx_t* keys,
            const float* coarse_dis,
            RangeSearchResult* result,
            bool store_pairs = false,
            const IVFSearchParameters* params = nullptr,
            IndexIVFStats* stats = nullptr) const = 0;

    virtual ~IndexIVFInterface() {}
};
objects.description: Abstract interface that extends Level1Quantizer with IVF search entry points operating on preassigned coarse list indices, for both k-NN and range search. Holds default search-time parameters nprobe and max_codes. Implemented by concrete IVF indices.

Concrete IVF index base class combining Index and IndexIVFInterface. Owns or references InvertedLists storage, manages code size, parallel search modes, optional DirectMap, residual encoding flag, and all CRUD/search methods around IVF including encode/decode, reconstruction, merging, and standalone codec interface. Abstract in encode_vectors; concrete subclasses must implement encoding. Ownership of invlists governed by own_invlists; destructor releases if owned.

objects.definition: struct RangeQueryResult;
objects.description: Forward declaration only. Represents per-query accumulator for range search results. No definition provided here; details unknown.

Collects runtime statistics for IVF searches, including counts and timing for quantization and list scanning. Provides reset and accumulation methods. A global instance indexIVF_stats aggregates stats.

Concrete IVF (inverted lists) index that stores full-precision float vectors in the lists (no product quantization). It derives from faiss::IndexIVF and provides methods to add, encode/decode, scan, and reconstruct vectors. Construction requires a coarse quantizer, dimensionality, number of lists, and metric. Implementation details (memory ownership, list layout) follow IndexIVF semantics but are not shown here.

Variant of IndexIVFFlat that deduplicates identical vectors. Maintains an instances multimap from stored IDs to other IDs sharing the same vector content. Overrides training to deduplicate the training set and provides custom search/add/remove behavior. Some operations are explicitly unimplemented here (range_search, update_vectors, reconstruct_from_offset).

Search-parameter bundle specialized for IVFPQ searches. Extends IVFSearchParameters with controls for table-scanning threshold and polysemous Hamming threshold. Construction/destruction is trivial; no ownership of external resources is implied.

An inverted-file index with Product Quantization (PQ) encoding of residuals. Owns a ProductQuantizer and optional precomputed distance tables for faster L2-by-residual search. Supports training, adding, encoding/decoding vectors, search scanning, and duplicate detection. Memory ownership: contains pq and precomputed_table by value; may use an external PolysemousTraining instance via pointer (not owned unless managed elsewhere).
direct_api_constructors: faiss::IndexIVFPQ::IndexIVFPQ(Index*, size_t, size_t, size_t, size_t, MetricType, bool)

objects.description: Holds thread-robust aggregated statistics for IndexIVFPQ operations, including refine counts, passes of Hamming filters, and timing counters. reset() reinitializes all counters. Does not own external resources.

LSH-based flat index storing binary signatures produced from vector sign bits. Inherits from faiss::IndexFlatCodes to store and search codes directly. Provides optional random rotation preprocessing (rrot) and threshold training for binarization. Public fields configure number of bits, rotation, and thresholding; thresholds can be transferred to a separate preprocessing transform. Construction and usage details beyond the interface are not present here.

Core HNSW index class providing a random-access Faiss Index with a hierarchical navigable small world (HNSW) graph overlay. Manages the HNSW link structure (field hnsw) and an optional sequential storage Index. Supports add/train/search/range_search/reset and utilities to build or adjust the level-0 graph. Construction requires dimension d and graph degree M or an existing storage Index. Ownership of storage is controlled by own_fields. Details like HNSW, DistanceComputer, and Index come from external headers.
HNSW index with a flat (uncompressed) vector storage backend. Inherits all HNSW behavior from IndexHNSW; constructors set up a flat storage for vectors.

Panorama-enhanced HNSWFlat variant that performs progressive distance refinement using partial sums and Cauchy–Schwarz bounds. Maintains per-vector cumulative sums (cum_sums) and a Panorama configuration. Overrides add/reset/permute_entries to manage Panorama-specific state. Search behavior differs from vanilla HNSW by inserting candidates with approximate bounds before full evaluation.

HNSW index with Product Quantization (PQ) compressed storage. Adds constructors to configure PQ (m, nbits) and overrides train to train the PQ codebooks. Search/add interfaces are inherited from IndexHNSW.

HNSW index with Scalar Quantizer (SQ) compressed storage. Constructors select the scalar quantizer type and graph parameters. Inherits add/search/train from IndexHNSW unless storage requires training in base class.

Two-level structure combining HNSW with a coarse quantizer/IVF-like layout for fast random access. Provides a method flip_to_ivf to convert to an IVF structure and overrides search to adapt to the two-level organization.

CPU HNSW variant interoperable with GPU CAGRA graphs. Supports a base-level-only mode to import a prebuilt k-NN graph from GpuIndexCagra and search it without upper levels; disables addition of new vectors in that mode. Allows selecting the underlying numeric storage type used for vectors/graph weights via numeric_type_.

NSG-backed nearest neighbor index. Inherits faiss::Index and adds an NSG graph (faiss::NSG) on top of an underlying storage index (Index* storage). Provides construction parameters (R, GK, build_type, NN-Descent params), build/add/train/search/reconstruct/reset APIs, and a validator for external KNN graphs. own_fields indicates ownership of the storage. nndescent_L is expected to be set to GK + 50 during construction. Details like memory ownership and lifecycle beyond own_fields are not fully documented here.

NSG index variant that uses a flat (brute-force) storage backend (IndexFlat) under the NSG graph for efficient traversal. Constructors allow default or dimension/R/metric configuration. Training behavior is inherited from IndexNSG and typically trivial for flat storage.

NSG index variant that uses a Product Quantization (PQ) storage backend under the NSG graph. Offers default and parameterized constructors specifying dimensionality, PQ configuration (pq_m, M, pq_nbits). Overrides train to handle PQ training requirements.

NSG index variant that uses a Scalar Quantizer (SQ) storage backend beneath the NSG graph. Constructors allow default or parameterized creation (dimension, quantizer type, M, metric). Training behavior is inherited unless specialized elsewhere.

Abstract base class for binary (bit-vector) indexes in Faiss. Manages binary vectors of dimension d bits (code_size = d/8), supports training, adding vectors (optionally with IDs), k-NN and range search, reconstruction, and merging. Uses MetricType (default METRIC_L2) for distance; distance_t is int32_t (e.g., Hamming count). Provides virtual interface; concrete implementations must implement add, search, reset; others may be overridden as needed. Note: constructors are declared but defined elsewhere; lifetime and ownership rules depend on derived classes.

Concrete binary index that stores full binary vectors in-memory and performs exhaustive search over them. It derives from faiss::IndexBinary (defined elsewhere) and keeps the dataset in xb as packed bytes of size ntotal * d / 8. It supports add, reset, exact and range search, reconstruction, and id removal with shifted ids. Tuning fields include use_heap, query_batch_size, and approx_topk_mode. Construction requires dimensionality d (bits). Ownership and destruction follow base-class semantics; memory for xb is managed by MaybeOwnedVector.

Binary-vector HNSW index combining an HNSW graph (member hnsw) with a binary IndexBinary storage back-end. Manages whether it owns the storage (own_fields) and allows configuring base-level graph initialization and saturation. Provides constructors to create an empty index by dimensionality/M, or to wrap an existing IndexBinary storage, and exposes standard FAISS index methods for add/train/search/reconstruct/reset. Details like HNSW parameters (e.g., M) are set via constructors; destruction will free owned storage when own_fields is true. Some behavior can be altered for GPU interop via init_level0 and keep_max_size_level0.

Specialized HNSW binary index tuned for interoperability with GPU CAGRA. Inherits IndexBinaryHNSW and adds options to operate with only the base-level graph (base_level_only) and to control entrypoint sampling for base-level-only search. Constructors allow dimension/M configuration. When base_level_only is true, the index is immutable and only searches the base layer; add may be disabled or behave differently.

Abstract base index wrapper that performs per-vector (rowwise) min–max normalization to [0,1] prior to delegating to a sub-index. It stores a pointer to the wrapped sub-index (index) and a flag (own_fields) indicating ownership for destruction. It overrides add, search, and reset to apply scaling logic around the sub-index calls, and defines a pure-virtual train_inplace to enable in-place scaling during training. Construction/destruction specifics are not detailed in this header; ownership semantics depend on own_fields.

Concrete rowwise min–max index that stores scaling coefficients per vector as fp16, adding 4 bytes per encoded vector. Provides training (with copy or in-place), and vector codec interface (sa_code_size/sa_encode/sa_decode) compatible with its sub-index. It wraps a sub-index via the IndexRowwiseMinMaxBase base class.

Concrete rowwise min–max index that stores scaling coefficients per vector as fp32, adding 8 bytes per encoded vector. Provides training (with copy or in-place) and vector codec methods, delegating core indexing to the wrapped sub-index via the base class.

Templated sharded index that aggregates and queries multiple sub-index shards of type IndexT, optionally in parallel via ThreadedIndex. It supports adding shards, adding vectors (with or without explicit ids), searching across shards, training, and synchronizing top-level metadata with sub-indexes. The bool member successive_ids controls whether returned ids are offset per-shard. Constructors allow unspecified dimension (derived from first shard) or explicit dimension. Details of memory ownership and threading behavior follow ThreadedIndex<IndexT> from Faiss.

Alias specialization of IndexShardsTemplate for binary indices (IndexBinary). Provides sharded behavior for binary vectors/distances. Same API and semantics as the primary template; component and distance types come from IndexBinary.
Note: This entry is a duplicate of the primary template and should not be separate. Please refer to the first object above.

Search-parameter bundle for IndexRefine-family searches. Adds a multiplicative k_factor to control how many candidates the base index retrieves before refinement, and optionally forwards a non-owning SearchParameters pointer to the base index. Exact ownership, lifetime, or additional behavior beyond these fields is not documented here.

Composite index that first queries a fast base_index to preselect candidates and then refines results using a refine_index (typically more accurate). own_fields and own_refine_index indicate whether the respective sub-index pointers are owned and should be deallocated by this instance. k_factor controls the multiplier between requested k and the number asked from the base index. Provides full Index overrides and standalone codec methods; reconstruct is delegated to refine_index.

Specialization of IndexRefine where the refinement index is an IndexFlat. Adds constructors, including one that accepts a pointer to training/adding data xb for initializing the flat refinement index. Overrides search with behavior tailored to the flat refine stage. Specifics of xb size/ownership are not documented here.

IndexRefine variant whose search path calls search_subset to support Panorama-style refinement. It forwards construction to IndexRefine and overrides search accordingly. Further operational details are not present in this header.

Vector index that stores product-quantized (PQ) codes. Inherits IndexFlatCodes and encodes vectors with an internal ProductQuantizer. Supports training, search, standalone encode/decode, and polysemous-code search variants (Hamming-based filtering/combination).
direct_api_constructors: faiss::IndexPQ::IndexPQ(int d, size_t M, size_t nbits, MetricType metric)

objects.description: Enumeration of search strategies used by IndexPQ: asymmetric PQ, Hamming-based, generalized Hamming, symmetric distance computation, and polysemous combinations.
Search-override parameters for IndexPQ searches. Lets callers specify the search_type and Hamming threshold (polysemous_ht).
Thread-robust statistics for IndexPQ usage (not safe if IndexPQ::search is concurrently invoked from multiple threads). Tracks number of queries, visited codes, and Hamming passes. Provides reset().
Index whose centroids are the Cartesian product of ProductQuantizer sub-centroids. Supports training, search, reconstruction; add/reset are intentionally unsupported at runtime per comment.
Variant of MultiIndexQuantizer that performs PQ assignment via sub-indexes over subspaces. Owns an array/vector of Index* used for assignment; own_fields indicates ownership semantics.
direct_api_constructors: faiss::MultiIndexQuantizer2::MultiIndexQuantizer2(int d, size_t M, size_t nbits, Index** indexes)
faiss::MultiIndexQuantizer2::MultiIndexQuantizer2(int d, size_t nbits, Index* assign_index_0, Index* assign_index_1)

objects.description: Specialized search-parameter holder for pre-transform searches. It inherits faiss::SearchParameters and optionally encapsulates another SearchParameters object (index_params) that will be forwarded to the wrapped sub-index after the transform chain. Details beyond this are not documented here; behavior mirrors base SearchParameters with an extra pointer that may be null.

Index adapter that owns a chain of VectorTransform objects applied to input vectors before delegating to a wrapped sub-index (index). Provides full Index interface: training, add, search, range search, reconstruction, standalone codec operations, merge, and compatibility checks. The own_fields flag indicates whether the transform pointers and sub-index are deleted by the destructor. Construction can be empty, with a sub-index, or with a last transform plus sub-index.

Abstract base class for transformations on d_in-dimensional float vectors producing d_out-dimensional outputs. Provides optional training, allocation and no-allocation apply paths, optional reverse transform, and an identity/equality check hook. is_trained indicates whether training is required or complete.

Concrete VectorTransform implementing a linear mapping y = A*x + b with optional bias and support for reverse transform when A has orthonormal rows. Holds A and b storage and utility methods to test orthonormality.
LinearTransform that applies a random rotation (and possible projection) between dimensions. init(seed) or train(...) initializes A; no bias is used.
LinearTransform implementing PCA with optional whitening (via eigen_power/epsilon) and optional post random rotation. Stores mean, eigenvalues, and PCA basis; training computes these and final A/b.

LinearTransform for Iterative Quantization (ITQ) rotation learning to produce balanced binary codes. Trains an orthogonal rotation with up to max_iter iterations; seed controls randomness; init_rotation can force initialization.

Composite VectorTransform that performs mean-centering, optional PCA, and an ITQ rotation to map inputs to d_out dimensions for binary coding. Holds an internal ITQMatrix and a composed LinearTransform for application.

LinearTransform implementing Optimized Product Quantization rotation/projection aligned to a ProductQuantizer with M subquantizers. Trains over several outer/inner iterations and can reuse an external ProductQuantizer. Produces a d_out mapping (optionally to d2).

VectorTransform that remaps or subsamples input dimensions to outputs according to a map, inserting zeros for -1 entries. Supports uniform distribution mode and a best-effort reverse when the map is a permutation.
VectorTransform that L_p-normalizes each input vector to the specified norm (default L2). Reverse transform is identity since normalization is not invertible.
VectorTransform that subtracts the per-dimension mean learned during training and can add it back in reverse. d_in equals d_out.

Abstract base class representing an evaluation criterion for ANN search quality. Holds query count, requested neighbors, required ground-truth neighbors, and ground-truth arrays. Subclasses implement evaluate() to produce a score in [0,1]. Ground truth must be set via set_groundtruth() before evaluation. Ownership: used by ParameterSpace::explore to assess performance.
Concrete criterion computing 1-recall@R (whether the first ground-truth neighbor is found within the top-R results). Initialized with number of queries and R. Uses base class ground-truth buffers.
Concrete criterion measuring the intersection between retrieved top-nnn and ground-truth top-R results across queries. Initialized with number of queries and R. Uses base class ground-truth buffers.
Plain data struct representing a single operating point in tuning: performance score, time in ms, an identifying key, and an optional configuration number.
Container for experimental operating points with utilities to merge, add, filter Pareto-optimal points, query time for a target performance, and export/display results.
Represents a tunable parameter and its candidate values, ordered from least to most expensive/accurate. Used by ParameterSpace to enumerate configurations.

Defines the tunable search parameter space for Faiss indexes and provides methods to enumerate combinations, initialize defaults for a given Index, apply parameter combinations to an Index, bound performance/time, and explore operating points against a criterion. Holds search/exploration controls like verbosity, number of experiments, batching, threading, and minimum test duration.

Parameter bundle configuring k-means clustering behavior (iterations, initialization, reproducibility, centroid post-processing, subsampling, etc.). Used to construct and control faiss::Clustering and derivatives.
Holds per-iteration statistics emitted by clustering runs (objective, timing, imbalance, splits).

Main k-means implementation operating over a faiss::Index for assignment. Stores centroids and iteration stats. Inherits configuration from ClusteringParameters. train() and train_encoded() perform fitting; post_process_centroids() applies optional normalization/rounding. Construction provided via ctors taking dimensionality, k, and optional parameters.
direct_api_constructors: faiss::Clustering::Clustering(int d, int k, const ClusteringParameters& cp)

objects.description: Exact 1D k-means variant that does not use an Index. Inherits all parameters and centroids handling from Clustering; provides train_exact() for one-dimensional data.

Parameter set for progressive-dimension clustering. Extends ClusteringParameters with number of incremental dimension steps and whether to apply PCA. Constructor presumably sets sensible defaults (not shown here).
Factory interface that creates a faiss::Index suitable for clustering at a given dimensionality; ownership of the created index is transferred to the caller.

K-means clustering variant that progressively increases the working dimensionality (optionally after PCA), maintaining centroids and iteration stats. Uses a ProgressiveDimIndexFactory to obtain indices at each step.
direct_api_constructors: faiss::ProgressiveDimClustering::ProgressiveDimClustering(int d, int k, const ProgressiveDimClusteringParameters& cp)

objects.description: Composite FAISS index that splits each input vector into contiguous segments and routes each segment to a corresponding sub-index held in sub_indexes. Useful to distribute a MultiIndexQuantizer or combine multiple indices whose dimensions sum to the overall dimensionality. own_fields indicates ownership of sub-indexes, threaded toggles multithreaded behavior, and sum_d tracks cumulative dimensions. Construction requires providing dimensionality d and optional threading flag; add_sub_index and sync_with_sub_indexes manage sub-index configuration. Supports add, search, train, and reset operations. Destruction behavior is defined in the implementation; ownership semantics depend on own_fields.

FAISS index that returns random search results, primarily for timing and benchmarking. It stores a seed for deterministic randomness. Constructor takes dimensionality d, an optional initial ntotal (number of vectors to pretend to contain), a random seed, and metric type. Implements add, search (random labels and distances according to mt), reconstruct (likely random or trivial), and reset. Not intended for accuracy; used to measure overhead.

objects.definition: FAISS_API extern int index_factory_verbose;
objects.description: Global verbosity flag for index_factory logging. When set to a value > 0, index_factory produces more logs. This is a variable, not a type; included here only as a named alias pointer per instructions.

objects.definition: struct Index;
objects.description: Forward declaration of the faiss::Index base type for vector indexes. Only an incomplete type is provided here; definition is elsewhere.

objects.definition: struct IndexBinary;
objects.description: Forward declaration of the faiss::IndexBinary base type for binary vector indexes. Only an incomplete type is provided here; definition is elsewhere.

objects.definition: struct VectorTransform;
objects.description: Forward declaration of a transformation applied to vectors (e.g., PCA, OPQ). Only an incomplete type is provided here; definition is elsewhere.

objects.definition: struct ProductQuantizer;
objects.description: Forward declaration of the ProductQuantizer component used for vector quantization. Only an incomplete type is provided here; definition is elsewhere.

objects.definition: struct IOReader;
objects.description: Forward declaration of an abstract input reader used by I/O helpers. Only an incomplete type is provided here; definition is elsewhere.

objects.definition: struct IOWriter;
objects.description: Forward declaration of an abstract output writer used by I/O helpers. Only an incomplete type is provided here; definition is elsewhere.

objects.definition: struct InvertedLists;
objects.description: Forward declaration of an inverted lists container used by IVF-based indexes. Only an incomplete type is provided here; definition is elsewhere.

Enumeration of supported distance/similarity metrics for Faiss. Values include inner product, L2/L1/Linf, generic Lp, and several specialized metrics (Canberra, Bray–Curtis, Jensen–Shannon, Jaccard, NaN-robust squared Euclidean, and Gower). Used by indices/algorithms to select scoring behavior. Details like Lp's p parameter are provided elsewhere (e.g., via an Index's metric_arg).

objects.definition: using idx_t = int64_t;
objects.description: Signed 64-bit integer type used for vector indices and identifiers throughout Faiss. Typedef alias to int64_t.

Struct that computes and stores statistics over an n-by-d float matrix, including per-vector norm bounds, counts of valid/zero entries, hash collisions, and detailed per-dimension statistics. It also accumulates human-readable comments. Provides nested types PerDimStats (to aggregate per-dimension counts and moments, with add() and compute_mean_std()) and Occurrence (to track first index and count for hashed rows). Implementation details of methods are not present in this header.
direct_api_constructors: faiss::MatrixStats::MatrixStats(size_t n, size_t d, const float* x)

objects.description: Nested struct inside faiss::MatrixStats that accumulates statistics for a single dimension across vectors: counts of NaN/Inf/zero, min/max, sums and sums of squares, and derived mean/stddev. Methods add() to incorporate a value and compute_mean_std() to finalize mean/stddev are declared but not defined here.

Nested struct inside faiss::MatrixStats used as the mapped value in the occurrences hash map. Tracks the first index observed and the total count of occurrences for a given 64-bit key (typically a row hash). No constructors or methods are defined in this header.

Adapter IDSelector that translates queried internal ids through an id_map before delegating to another selector sel. It references the id_map from an IndexIDMap/IndexBinaryIDMap or a provided vector. Useful for delete operations where external ids are used.

Flat, two-layer product-quantized index that stores encoded vectors sequentially without inverted lists. Intended for random access to encoded codes rather than ANN search (search is declared but not implemented). Wraps a first-level quantizer (coarse, Level1Quantizer) and a second-level ProductQuantizer; exposes training and standalone encode/decode of vectors to byte codes, ability to transfer stored codes to an IndexIVFPQ. Ownership/usage details: derives from IndexFlatCodes and manages code size bookkeeping. Construction can be via a default constructor or a configured constructor taking a coarse quantizer, number of lists, PQ parameters, and metric. Destruction is virtual via base. Some operational details (e.g., exact search behavior) are not implemented in this class.
direct_api_constructors: faiss::Index2Layer::Index2Layer(Index* quantizer, size_t nlist, int M, int nbit, MetricType metric)

objects.definition: FAISS_API extern int index2layer_sa_encode_bs;
objects.description: Global parameter controlling the block size used by Index2Layer::sa_encode. Declared extern in this header; definition is provided elsewhere. It is a tunable integer affecting encoding performance/tiling.

Binary index adapter that exposes the IndexBinary interface while delegating storage/search to an underlying float (real-valued) faiss::Index via the index field. It allows adding, training, and searching binary vectors by converting/bridging to the float index. The own_fields flag indicates whether this object is responsible for deleting the underlying index in the destructor. Exact conversion details and metric handling are not specified in this header.

objects.definition: struct Index;
objects.description: Forward declaration of a float (real-valued) Faiss index type used by IndexBinaryFromFloat. Only declared here; definition lives elsewhere.

Panorama-adapted variant of faiss::IndexIVFFlat that changes per-list storage layout and uses level-based pruning bounds to accelerate search. Stores cumulative residual energy per vector across n_levels to enable pruning; adds (n_levels + 1) floats per stored vector. Construction mirrors IndexIVFFlat with an added n_levels parameter. The actual level-oriented storage lives in ArrayInvertedListsPanorama owned by the base IndexIVF; this class configures/uses it and provides a specialized inverted list scanner and reconstruction from list offsets. Details like ownership semantics of cum_sums and interaction with MaybeOwnedVector are inferred; exact behavior beyond the provided declaration is unknown in this header.

Fast-scan quantized vector index specialized for 4-bit PQ/AQ codes. Codes are stored in SIMD-friendly blocks (bbs) to accelerate distance computations. Provides Index-compatible API (add, search, reconstruct, remove_ids, merge) and abstract hooks to compute codes and floating-point lookup tables. Maintains packed codes, code sizes, and internal parameters controlling implementations and block sizes. Derived classes must implement compute_codes and compute_float_LUT.

Lightweight timing/diagnostics structure with four timestamp counters (t0–t3) and a reset method that zeroes all fields. An extern global FastScan_stats instance is declared for collecting stats; it is defined elsewhere.

Concrete FAISS index class derived from IndexIVF implementing a fast-scan IVF with SIMD-friendly packed codes for 4-bit PQ/AQ. Provides construction, LUT computation, search (KNN and range), decoding, and specialized dispatch/implementation hooks. Contains an embedded helper struct CoarseQuantized for passing coarse-quantization results. Some behavior is abstract (lookup_table_is_3d, compute_LUT) and must be implemented by subclasses. Construction/destruction follow FAISS ownership rules inherited from IndexIVF; fine_quantizer is an external Quantizer pointer not owned unless specified by parent flags. Details like memory ownership of orig_invlists are not fully specified in this header.
Compact POD used to pass coarse-quantization results (IDs of probed lists and their distances) to LUT computation and scanning routines within IndexIVFFastScan.

Instrumentation structure collecting timing counters for fast-scan operations and helper methods to convert counters to milliseconds-equivalent units. A global extern instance IVFFastScan_stats is declared for module-wide stats. Ownership and lifetime of the extern instance are outside this header.

Search-time parameter bundle for RaBitQ indices. Extends faiss::SearchParameters by adding quantization controls: qb is the number of bits to quantize queries with (0 disables query quantization), and centered selects zero-centered scalar quantization. Other inherited SearchParameters fields (if any) are available via the base class. Exact destruction/ownership follows standard struct semantics; no special lifetime management is required.

A FAISS flat, code-based index using RaBit (random bit) quantization for storage and optionally for query-time quantization. Inherits from IndexFlatCodes, storing encoded vectors and providing train/encode/decode, k-NN search, and range search. Fields: rabitq (RaBitQuantizer instance managing codebook/quantization), center (training-set centroid used for centered quantization), qb (default query quantization bits, 0 means use raw float queries), centered (toggle for zero-centered scalar quantization). Constructors provide default and parameterized creation with dimensionality, metric (default L2), and number of bits. Destruction follows base-class semantics; no custom destructor declared here. Usage notes: prefer get_FlatCodesDistanceComputer or get_quantized_distance_computer for distance computation; sa_decode may be suboptimal for L2 as noted in comments.

Search-parameter bundle for IndexIVFRaBitQ. Extends IVFSearchParameters by adding qb (number of bits used to quantize the query; 0 disables query quantization) and centered (whether query quantization is centered). Other IVFSearchParameters fields are inherited but not shown here.

An IVF (inverted file) index variant using RaBitQuantizer for product-like residual bit quantization. Owns a RaBitQuantizer and supports training/encoding/decoding residuals, adding vectors, scanning lists, and distance computation. Field qb sets default query quantization bits (0 to disable). Constructs with an IVF coarse quantizer, dimensionality d, number of lists nlist, metric, list-ownership flag, and nb_bits for the encoder. Destruction/ownership follow IndexIVF conventions (e.g., own_invlists governs inverted list lifetime).

objects.description: Fast-scan IVF index variant combining IVF with RaBitQ quantization. Owns RaBitQuantizer and flat per-vector auxiliary storage; overrides FastScan paths to compute LUTs, encode, and search with RaBitQ-specific handling. Constructors mirror IVF setup and conversion from IndexIVFRaBitQ. Destruction/ownership follows base IndexIVFFastScan semantics; no custom destructor declared.

objects.description: Fast-scan variant of FAISS IVF-PQ index specialized for 4-bit PQ codes using block-based storage (bbs) to enable SIMD-accelerated distance computation. It derives from faiss::IndexIVFFastScan and embeds a ProductQuantizer, optional precomputed distance tables, and overrides encoder/training and LUT-related methods. Constructors allow building from parameters or converting from an existing IndexIVFPQ. Exact ownership, destruction, and memory management follow FAISS Index conventions via the base class; the header does not document additional constraints beyond block size and optional precomputation.

objects.description: faiss IVF index variant that adds a third-level refinement with a ProductQuantizer. It inherits from IndexIVFPQ and stores an additional refine_pq and its codes to re-rank or refine results. Contains training, add, search, and maintenance methods overriding the base. Details of memory ownership and lifecycle follow base class semantics; unknown specifics beyond fields shown.
direct_api_constructors: faiss::IndexIVFPQR::IndexIVFPQR(Index*, size_t, size_t, size_t, size_t, size_t, size_t, bool)

objects.description: IVF index variant that applies a VectorTransform to map input vectors from dimension d to nbit, then encodes each transformed coordinate into a binary signature using a periodic thresholding scheme (spectral hashing). Supports several thresholding strategies via ThresholdType, stores optional trained thresholds per list/bit, and integrates with FAISS’s IVF search pipeline. Owns an optional VectorTransform (vt) when own_fields is true. Construction requires an IVF quantizer, dimensions, code size (nbit), and period. Destruction and other lifecycle aspects follow IndexIVF; vt ownership depends on own_fields. Details of storage and scanning use IndexIVF mechanisms.

objects.description: Enumeration of spectral-hash thresholding strategies controlling how each transformed coordinate is binarized. Used as IndexIVFSpectralHash::threshold_type. Not independently constructible; lives within IndexIVFSpectralHash.

faiss::IndexLattice is an index type that encodes vectors using a sequence of Zn lattice quantizers. It derives from faiss::IndexFlatCodes and adds configuration for sub-vector partitioning (nsq, dsq), lattice codec (ZnSphereCodecAlt), bit allocation for scale and lattice, and training statistics. Suitable for compressed representation and standalone encode/decode via the sa_* interface. Details about codec internals and exact encoding format are defined elsewhere (unknown from this header).

Random-access Faiss index that augments a base Index with an NN-Descent graph for faster neighbor search. Owns an NNDescent link structure and either owns or references an underlying storage Index. Provides add, train, search, reconstruct, and reset overrides. Details like exact graph parameters beyond K and metric are defined elsewhere.
Convenience subclass of IndexNNDescent that uses a flat (brute-force) storage backend with an NN-Descent overlay. Constructors provide default and parameterized initialization.

Abstract base index for additive quantizers, extending IndexFlatCodes. Holds a pointer to an AdditiveQuantizer and implements shared search/standalone codec entry points for derived additive-quantizer indexes.
Index whose codes are produced by a ResidualQuantizer. Provides training and uses additive-quantizer search codec from the base. Supports uniform or per-level nbits construction.
Index based on LocalSearchQuantizer codes. Trains LSQ and leverages additive-quantizer search/codec methods from the base.
Index using a ProductResidualQuantizer (multiple residual quantizers over splits). Supports training and construction with split parameters.
Index using a ProductLocalSearchQuantizer across splits. Provides constructors and training; search/codec routes through base class.

Coarse quantizer index whose list of elements corresponds to additive-quantizer centroids. Intended for IVF coarse quantization; stores centroid norms and delegates search/training to additive quantizer centroids.
Search parameters bundle for ResidualCoarseQuantizer that carries a beam_factor to control beam search vs k. Used at search time to tune residual coarse quantizer behavior.

Coarse index specialized for ResidualQuantizer centroids. Supports beam search via beam_factor, adjustable with set_beam_factor, and provides constructors for uniform or per-level nbits as well as copy-initialization of leading codebook levels.
Coarse quantizer variant built on LocalSearchQuantizer centroids. Provides constructors; search/training are inherited from AdditiveCoarseQuantizer.

Abstract IVF index that stores compressed vectors using an AdditiveQuantizer. Provides common training, encoding/decoding, scanning, and reconstruction hooks on top of IndexIVF. Holds a pointer to an AdditiveQuantizer (not owned semantics unspecified here).

IVF index variant that uses a ResidualQuantizer (owned as 'rq' member) to encode stored vectors with residual quantization codes. Suitable when residual quantization fits data; exposes constructors for per-subquantizer nbits or uniform settings.

objects.description: Concrete faiss::Index variant that composes an IVF index where the coarse quantizer operates on a (potentially different) input dimension from the stored payload. Input vectors may be preprocessed by an optional VectorTransform before being routed to the internal IndexIVF. Fields: quantizer (coarse quantizer over raw inputs), vt (optional transform), index_ivf (IVF container controlling nlist/nprobe), own_fields (ownership flag). Lifecycle: provides train, add, search, reset; destructor may free subcomponents if own_fields is true. Base type Index, and referenced types IndexIVF, VectorTransform, idx_t, SearchParameters are declared elsewhere.

Fast-scan FAISS index that wraps an AdditiveQuantizer for 4-bit AQ (and related) with SIMD-friendly blocked storage. Provides training, coding, LUT computation, search, and decoding. Inherits from IndexFastScan. Holds a non-owning pointer to an AdditiveQuantizer and exposes configuration like rescale_norm, norm_scale, and max_train_points. Construction can be from an AdditiveQuantizer pointer or from an existing IndexAdditiveQuantizer. Ownership semantics of aq are not explicit here; refer to implementation to know whether this class owns or references the quantizer.

Fast-scan index specialized for residual quantization. Inherits IndexAdditiveQuantizerFastScan and owns an embedded ResidualQuantizer used to encode vectors. Provides constructors to create an index given dimensionality and RQ parameters.
Fast-scan index specialized for local search quantization (LSQ). Inherits IndexAdditiveQuantizerFastScan and embeds a LocalSearchQuantizer. Offers constructors with LSQ parameters.
Fast-scan index for product residual quantization (PRQ). Inherits IndexAdditiveQuantizerFastScan and owns a ProductResidualQuantizer, parameterized by number of splits and subquantizers per split.

Fast-scan index for product local search quantization (PLSQ). Inherits IndexAdditiveQuantizerFastScan and embeds a ProductLocalSearchQuantizer, parameterized by number of splits and subquantizers per split.

Fast-scan IVF index using an AdditiveQuantizer backend. Stores inverted-list codes in SIMD-friendly blocks (bbs) to accelerate distance computation, currently targeting 4-bit AQ. Provides training, encoding, and search with specialized LUT computation and optional norm rescaling. Inherits IndexIVFFastScan. Construction requires an IVF coarse quantizer and an AdditiveQuantizer. Destructor is virtual and overridden.

Provides constructors to set topology (nsplits, Msub), bit-width, metric, and search type. Inherits fast-scan mechanisms from the additive-quantizer base.

Constructors expose structural, bit-width, metric, and search-type parameters. Inherits fast-scan encode/search and LUT logic from the additive-quantizer base.

objects.description: An index implementation that stores fixed-length codes using a neural-network-based codec. It extends IndexFlatCodes to encode/decode vectors via a NeuralNetCodec and supports training and symmetric distance computation defined by the base. Fields: net (owned pointer to the neural codec; ownership/lifecycle not specified here), M and nbits (code structure hyperparameters). Constructor allows dimension, M, nbits, and metric selection. Provides training, and vector encode/decode overrides. Destruction is trivial here; responsibility for net may be handled elsewhere (unclear from header).

A specialized IndexNeuralNetCodec that embeds a QINCo neural network codec instance as a value member. Intended to configure and use QINCo with parameters L and h in addition to base parameters d, M, nbits, and metric. Destructor is trivial; ownership of qinco is direct. Construction likely initializes the embedded codec; details are not present here.

A helper struct managing a FIFO window of concatenated IndexIVF slices inside a common parent Index. It tracks inverted lists (ils), number of active slices, nlist, and cumulative list sizes, and provides step() to add a new slice and optionally evict the oldest. Construction requires an already trained, initially empty index.

Abstract functor interface to map an item index i to a shard in [0, shard_count). Used to partition IVF centroids/files. Provides virtual call operator and defaulted special members for value semantics.
Concrete ShardingFunction that implements a default sharding policy (implied to be i mod shard_count). Suitable for use with centroid sharding helpers.

objects.description: Type alias binding IndexReplicasTemplate to faiss::Index for floating-point (or standard) FAISS indices; represents a replica manager for faiss::Index instances.

objects.definition: using IndexBinaryReplicas = IndexReplicasTemplate<IndexBinary>;
objects.description: Type alias binding IndexReplicasTemplate to faiss::IndexBinary for binary FAISS indices; represents a replica manager for faiss::IndexBinary instances.

Sharded FAISS index that shares a single coarse (level-1) quantizer across all shards. It derives from IndexShards and Level1Quantizer, requiring that added shard indexes implement the IVF interface so precomputed coarse assignments can be used during search. Provides constructors and overrides for adding shard indexes, training, adding vectors with IDs, and searching. Details of ownership semantics and lifetime management of child indexes/quantizer are not shown here and must be inferred from FAISS conventions.

Concrete faiss::Index subclass that stores all vectors as fixed-size byte codes of length code_size inside a MaybeOwnedVector<uint8_t> called codes. Provides add/search/range_search/reconstruction by encoding/decoding, supports removal (with shifted ids), merging from other indices, permutation of entries, and creation of a CodePacker and a FlatCodesDistanceComputer. Implementation details (actual encoding/decoding scheme) are not present in this header.

Fast-scan variant of faiss::IndexPQ specialized for 4-bit product quantization with block-based code layout to accelerate distance computations via SIMD. Inherits from IndexFastScan and embeds a ProductQuantizer (pq). Provides constructors for dimension/quantizer configuration or from an existing IndexPQ, and overrides training, code computation, LUT computation, and semi-asymmetric decode. Internal details like heap/reservoir accumulators and blocked loops are implied by comments; exact algorithms live in the implementation file.

Binary index that hashes vectors using the first b bits as the hash key. Maintains an unordered_map from hash value to an InvertedList storing ids and raw binary codes. Supports add, add_with_ids, search, and range_search with optional bit-flip probing (nflip). Construction requires dimensionality d and hash bits b. Destruction/ownership follows IndexBinary semantics; no special destructor is declared.

Container for one hash bucket within IndexBinaryHash. Stores vector ids and concatenated binary codes (vecs). add appends an id and its code of size code_size. Lifetime is managed by IndexBinaryHash via its unordered_map.

Holds runtime statistics for IndexBinaryHash queries: number of queries, empty lists encountered, lists scanned, and distances computed. Provides reset() and a default constructor that resets. A global extern instance indexBinaryHash_stats is declared; definition is elsewhere.

Binary index that uses multiple hash tables (nhash), each with b bits, to index binary vectors. Stores vectors in an IndexBinaryFlat pointed to by storage, with ownership controlled by own_fields. Each hash table maps from hash value to a vector of ids. Supports add, search, and range_search with optional probing via nflip. Provides destructor, reset, and hashtable_size.

Flat index implementation that stores codes produced by a ScalarQuantizer and supports training, encoding/decoding, and searching using the selected metric. It derives from IndexFlatCodes and embeds a ScalarQuantizer (sq) used to encode vectors. Construction requires dimensionality and quantizer type; an overload provides a default constructor. Details of memory ownership and lifecycle follow IndexFlatCodes/Index; specific destruction details are not present in this header.

IVF (inverted file) index variant whose residuals are encoded with a ScalarQuantizer. All search distances are computed asymmetrically by decoding approximate vectors. Inherits from IndexIVF and embeds a ScalarQuantizer (sq). Constructors allow specifying an external coarse quantizer, dimensionality, number of lists, quantizer type, metric, residual encoding, and ownership of inverted lists. Precise memory ownership semantics follow IndexIVF; not detailed here.

On unsupported/unknown numeric_type the function throws (FAISS_THROW_MSG)

metric must be a valid faiss::MetricType understood by the index implementation

functions.signature: virtual faiss::Index::~Index()

requirements: Derived classes should ensure proper resource release in their destructors

functions.name: faiss::Index::train
functions.signature: virtual void faiss::Index::train(idx_t n, const float* x)
functions.description: Trains the index on a representative set of vectors. Required by index types that need training prior to adding/searching. x is an n*d row-major matrix of float32.
requirements: If the index requires training, this must be called before add/search (check is_trained)
x must point to at least n*d floats, laid out row-major
n may be 0 only if the specific index supports empty training (not specified here)
d must match the index dimension set at construction

requirements: x must contain n*d elements of the specified numeric_type in row-major layout
numeric_type must be Float32 in the default base implementation; otherwise an exception is thrown
d must match the index dimension

x must point to at least n*d floats, row-major
d must match the index dimension
May be called with n=0 if supported by implementation (not specified)

requirements: x must contain n*d elements of the specified numeric_type in row-major layout
numeric_type must be Float32 in the default base implementation; otherwise an exception is thrown

functions.name: faiss::Index::search
functions.signature: virtual void faiss::Index::search(idx_t n, const float* x, idx_t k, float* distances, idx_t* labels, const faiss::SearchParameters* params = nullptr) const = 0
functions.description: Performs k-NN search for n queries. For each query in x (n*d matrix), returns up to k nearest neighbors’ distances and labels. If there are not enough results, pads labels with -1. Pure virtual; implemented by concrete indexes. Optional params can restrict candidates, etc.
requirements: x must point to at least n*d floats, row-major
distances must point to at least n*k floats for output
labels must point to at least n*k ids for output
k must be >= 1 (not explicitly stated, but implied by “number of extracted vectors”)
params, if provided, must point to a valid SearchParameters object whose lifetime spans the call
Index must contain data (ntotal may be 0, which can yield -1 padding)
d must match the index dimension

functions.name: faiss::Index::search_ex
functions.signature: virtual void faiss::Index::search_ex(idx_t n, const void* x, faiss::NumericType numeric_type, idx_t k, float* distances, idx_t* labels, const faiss::SearchParameters* params = nullptr) const

requirements: x must contain n*d elements of the specified numeric_type in row-major layout

distances must have space for n*k floats; labels for n*k ids
params, if provided, must remain valid during the call

result must be a valid, prepared RangeSearchResult object for n queries

key must correspond to an existing vector id in the index
Function may not be supported by all indexes; unsupported cases may throw or assert

functions.name: faiss::Index::reconstruct_batch
functions.signature: virtual void faiss::Index::reconstruct_batch(idx_t n, const idx_t* keys, float* recons) const
functions.description: Reconstructs stored vectors for a batch of n keys into recons (size n*d). Equivalent to multiple calls to reconstruct. May not be defined for some indexes.
requirements: keys must point to at least n ids
recons must point to at least n*d floats for output
All keys should correspond to existing vector ids
Function may not be supported by all indexes

functions.name: faiss::Index::reconstruct_n
functions.signature: virtual void faiss::Index::reconstruct_n(idx_t i0, idx_t ni, float* recons) const
functions.description: Reconstructs a contiguous sequence of ni vectors with internal indices i0..i0+ni-1 into recons (size ni*d). May not be defined for some indexes.
requirements: recons must point to at least ni*d floats
i0 and ni must define a valid range within the stored dataset
Function may not be supported by all indexes

functions.name: faiss::Index::search_and_reconstruct
functions.signature: virtual void faiss::Index::search_and_reconstruct(idx_t n, const float* x, idx_t k, float* distances, idx_t* labels, float* recons, const faiss::SearchParameters* params = nullptr) const
functions.description: Performs k-NN search for n queries and also reconstructs the found vectors into recons (shape n*k*d). If insufficient results, labels are padded with -1. Reconstructions may be approximate for lossy-coded indexes.
requirements: x must point to at least n*d floats, row-major
distances must have space for n*k floats; labels for n*k ids
recons must have space for n*k*d floats
k must be >= 1
params, if provided, must remain valid during the call

functions.name: faiss::Index::search_subset
functions.signature: virtual void faiss::Index::search_subset(idx_t n, const float* x, idx_t k_base, const idx_t* base_labels, idx_t k, float* distances, idx_t* labels) const
functions.description: Performs k-NN search for each query over a per-query subset of the database specified by base_labels (k_base candidates per query), returning top-k results. Not supported by all indexes; default implementation fails with an assertion.
requirements: x must point to at least n*d floats, row-major
base_labels must point to at least n*k_base ids specifying the candidate set for each query
distances must have space for n*k floats; labels for n*k ids
k_base must be >= k for meaningful results (not explicitly required but typical)
Implementation must support subset search; otherwise expect an assertion failure

functions.name: faiss::Index::compute_residual
functions.signature: virtual void faiss::Index::compute_residual(const float* x, float* residual, idx_t key) const
functions.description: Computes the residual vector for x relative to the reconstruction corresponding to key: residual = x - decode(key). Used in multi-stage indexing pipelines.
requirements: x must point to at least d floats
residual must point to at least d floats for output
key should be a valid encoded index (e.g., returned by search/assign) for the current index
Function support depends on the index; unsupported cases may throw/assert

functions.name: faiss::Index::compute_residual_n
functions.signature: virtual void faiss::Index::compute_residual_n(idx_t n, const float* xs, float* residuals, const idx_t* keys) const
functions.description: Batch version of compute_residual for n vectors. Computes residuals[i] = xs[i] - decode(keys[i]) for each i.
requirements: xs must point to at least n*d floats, row-major
residuals must point to at least n*d floats for output
keys must point to at least n ids valid for the index
Function support depends on the index; unsupported cases may throw/assert

functions.name: faiss::Index::get_distance_computer
functions.signature: virtual faiss::DistanceComputer* faiss::Index::get_distance_computer() const
functions.description: Returns a DistanceComputer instance suitable for this index type, for random access distance computations when supported.
requirements: Caller assumes ownership/lifetime semantics per implementation (not specified here)
May return nullptr or throw if the index does not support random access distance computation

functions.name: faiss::Index::sa_code_size
functions.signature: virtual size_t faiss::Index::sa_code_size() const
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of standalone codec codes produced/consumed by sa_encode/sa_decode for this index.
requirements: Must only be used with sa_encode/sa_decode on the same index type/configuration

functions.name: faiss::Index::sa_encode
functions.signature: virtual void faiss::Index::sa_encode(idx_t n, const float* x, uint8_t* bytes) const
functions.description: Encodes n float32 vectors x (n*d) into standalone codec byte codes of size n * sa_code_size().
requirements: x must point to at least n*d floats, row-major
bytes must point to a buffer of at least n * sa_code_size() bytes
Index must support standalone codec operations; otherwise may throw/assert

functions.name: faiss::Index::sa_decode
functions.signature: virtual void faiss::Index::sa_decode(idx_t n, const uint8_t* bytes, float* x) const
functions.description: Decodes n standalone codec byte codes into float32 vectors x (n*d).
requirements: bytes must point to at least n * sa_code_size() bytes
x must point to at least n*d floats for output
Index must support standalone codec operations; otherwise may throw/assert

functions.name: faiss::Index::merge_from
functions.signature: virtual void faiss::Index::merge_from(faiss::Index& otherIndex, idx_t add_id = 0)
functions.description: Moves all entries from otherIndex into this index, leaving otherIndex empty. Adds add_id to all moved ids (useful to offset sequential IDs).
requirements: This and otherIndex must be compatible; caller should call check_compatible_for_merge beforehand
otherIndex becomes empty after the call; its previous data should not be used
add_id should be chosen to avoid id collisions

functions.name: faiss::Index::check_compatible_for_merge
functions.signature: virtual void faiss::Index::check_compatible_for_merge(const faiss::Index& otherIndex) const
functions.description: Verifies that two indexes are compatible for merging (trained similarly and parameters match). Throws if not compatible.
requirements: otherIndex must be an index trained/configured identically to this
Caller should handle exceptions on incompatibility before calling merge_from

functions.name: faiss::Index::add_sa_codes
functions.signature: virtual void faiss::Index::add_sa_codes(idx_t n, const uint8_t* codes, const idx_t* xids)
functions.description: Adds n vectors to the index using precomputed standalone codec codes (size n*sa_code_size()), with corresponding ids xids.
requirements: codes must point to at least n * sa_code_size() bytes
xids must point to at least n ids
Index must support standalone codec ingestion; otherwise may throw/assert
Caller must ensure provided codes are compatible with this index’s codec parameters

functions.name: faiss::IndexFlat::IndexFlat
functions.signature: explicit faiss::IndexFlat::IndexFlat(idx_t d, MetricType metric = METRIC_L2);
functions.description: Constructs an exhaustive flat index that stores full vectors in float format and searches using the specified metric (default L2). Intended for cases where exact search over all stored vectors is acceptable.
requirements: d must be the dimensionality of all vectors subsequently added or queried with this index.
metric must be a valid faiss::MetricType understood by IndexFlat (typically METRIC_L2 or METRIC_INNER_PRODUCT).
The index is empty upon construction; callers must add vectors before searching.

functions.name: faiss::IndexFlat::IndexFlat
functions.signature: faiss::IndexFlat::IndexFlat();
functions.description: Default constructor for an empty IndexFlat. The dimensionality and metric are expected to be set by the base class or later initialization in implementation-specific ways.
requirements: Until properly initialized (dimension set and metric chosen), operations like add/search are not valid; usage details are implementation-defined.
After construction, ensure the index's dimensionality matches any vectors added or queried.

functions.name: faiss::IndexFlat::search
functions.signature: void faiss::IndexFlat::search(idx_t n, const float* x, idx_t k, float* distances, idx_t* labels, const SearchParameters* params = nullptr) const;
functions.description: Performs exhaustive k-nearest-neighbor search for n query vectors x against the stored database vectors, writing the top-k distances and corresponding vector IDs.
requirements: x must point to an array of size n * d, where d is the index dimensionality.
distances must point to an array of size n * k for the output distances.
labels must point to an array of size n * k for the output indices.
k must be >= 1 and <= number of database vectors (ntotal) to get fully valid results; if larger, excess results may be invalid or set to sentinel values depending on implementation.
params, if non-null, must point to a valid SearchParameters struct compatible with IndexFlat; unknown fields are ignored.
The index must have at least 1 vector added before search to produce meaningful results; with zero vectors, labels/distances outputs are implementation-defined.
Pointers may be null only when n == 0.

functions.name: faiss::IndexFlat::range_search
functions.signature: void faiss::IndexFlat::range_search(idx_t n, const float* x, float radius, RangeSearchResult* result, const SearchParameters* params = nullptr) const;
functions.description: Performs exhaustive range search for n query vectors x, returning all database vectors within the given radius per query via a RangeSearchResult accumulator.
requirements: x must point to an array of size n * d.
result must point to a valid, initialized RangeSearchResult able to collect results for n queries.
radius must be non-negative and interpreted under the Index metric (L2 radius or inner-product threshold semantics depending on metric).
params, if non-null, must be a valid SearchParameters instance compatible with IndexFlat.
Pointers may be null only when n == 0 (result must still be valid to receive zero results).

functions.name: faiss::IndexFlat::reconstruct
functions.signature: void faiss::IndexFlat::reconstruct(idx_t key, float* recons) const;
functions.description: Reconstructs and returns the stored vector with ID key into the output buffer.
requirements: key must refer to a valid stored vector ID in the index (0 <= key < ntotal).
recons must point to a buffer of size d to receive the reconstructed vector.
The index must contain at least (key+1) vectors.
Pointer recons must be non-null.

functions.name: faiss::IndexFlat::compute_distance_subset
functions.signature: void faiss::IndexFlat::compute_distance_subset(idx_t n, const float* x, idx_t k, float* distances, const idx_t* labels) const;
functions.description: Computes distances between each of the n query vectors and a specified subset of k database vectors per query, identified by labels, and writes the resulting distances.
requirements: x must point to query vectors of size n * d.
labels must point to an array of size n * k containing database indices to compare for each query.
distances must point to an array of size n * k to receive distances.
Each label in labels must be a valid database ID (0 <= id < ntotal).
k must be >= 1; n may be zero to perform no computation.
All pointers must be non-null unless n == 0.

functions.name: faiss::IndexFlat::get_xb
functions.signature: float* faiss::IndexFlat::get_xb();
functions.description: Returns a mutable pointer to the raw stored vector data as floats. For IndexFlat, codes are stored as raw float arrays, so this is a direct view.
requirements: The returned pointer remains valid as long as the underlying storage is not reallocated (e.g., by add/reset/resize).
Callers must not read/write past ntotal * d elements.
Modifying the returned buffer changes the index contents and must preserve the expected memory layout (row-major, contiguous).

functions.name: faiss::IndexFlat::get_xb
functions.signature: const float* faiss::IndexFlat::get_xb() const;
functions.description: Returns a const pointer to the raw stored vector data as floats. For IndexFlat, codes are stored as raw float arrays, so this is a direct view.
requirements: The returned pointer remains valid as long as the underlying storage is not reallocated (e.g., by add/reset/resize).
Do not read past ntotal * d elements.
The data layout is contiguous row-major with stride d.

functions.name: faiss::IndexFlat::get_FlatCodesDistanceComputer
functions.signature: FlatCodesDistanceComputer* faiss::IndexFlat::get_FlatCodesDistanceComputer() const;
functions.description: Returns a distance computer object specialized for the flat codes storage, used internally to compute distances between queries and stored vectors.
requirements: Return value is owned by the caller or the index depending on implementation; typical FAISS pattern returns a heap-allocated object that the caller must delete after use. If uncertain, consult implementation.
May return nullptr on allocation failure or unsupported configuration.

functions.name: faiss::IndexFlat::sa_encode
functions.signature: void faiss::IndexFlat::sa_encode(idx_t n, const float* x, uint8_t* bytes) const;
functions.description: Standalone codec: encodes n float vectors into raw byte codes. For IndexFlat, this is a direct memcpy of float data into the byte buffer.
requirements: x must point to an array of size n * d floats.
bytes must point to a buffer of at least n * code_size bytes, where code_size == d * sizeof(float) for IndexFlat.
Pointers must be non-null unless n == 0.
Endianness and float format must match the platform’s expectations (no conversion performed).

functions.name: faiss::IndexFlat::sa_decode
functions.signature: void faiss::IndexFlat::sa_decode(idx_t n, const uint8_t* bytes, float* x) const;
functions.description: Standalone codec: decodes n byte codes into float vectors. For IndexFlat, this is a direct memcpy from the byte buffer into floats.
requirements: bytes must point to a buffer of at least n * code_size bytes containing encoded vectors (code_size == d * sizeof(float) for IndexFlat).
x must point to an array of size n * d floats to receive the decoded data.
Pointers must be non-null unless n == 0.
The encoded data must have been produced with compatible endianness and float representation.

functions.name: faiss::IndexFlatIP::IndexFlatIP
functions.signature: explicit faiss::IndexFlatIP::IndexFlatIP(idx_t d);
functions.description: Constructs a flat index configured for inner-product similarity with dimensionality d.
requirements: d must match the dimensionality of all vectors added/searched.
Index is empty after construction; add vectors before searching.

functions.name: faiss::IndexFlatIP::IndexFlatIP
functions.signature: faiss::IndexFlatIP::IndexFlatIP();
functions.description: Default constructor for an inner-product flat index. Dimensionality must be established before use; specifics depend on implementation.
requirements: Do not add or search until the index dimensionality is set/initialized.
All vectors used later must match the established dimensionality.

functions.name: faiss::IndexFlatL2::IndexFlatL2
functions.signature: explicit faiss::IndexFlatL2::IndexFlatL2(idx_t d);
functions.description: Constructs a flat index configured for L2 (squared Euclidean) distance with dimensionality d. Supports optional cached L2 norms to speed computations.
requirements: d must match all vectors’ dimensionality.
Index is empty after construction; add vectors before searching.

functions.name: faiss::IndexFlatL2::IndexFlatL2
functions.signature: faiss::IndexFlatL2::IndexFlatL2();
functions.description: Default constructor for an L2 flat index. Dimensionality must be set before use; specifics depend on implementation.
requirements: Do not use add/search until dimensionality is set/initialized.
All vectors later must match the established dimensionality.

functions.name: faiss::IndexFlatL2::get_FlatCodesDistanceComputer
functions.signature: FlatCodesDistanceComputer* faiss::IndexFlatL2::get_FlatCodesDistanceComputer() const;
functions.description: Returns a distance computer optimized for L2 distance. If cached L2 norms are available, the returned computer may use dot-products plus norms for faster evaluation.
requirements: Ownership/lifetime follows FAISS distance computer conventions; caller may need to delete the returned object—consult implementation.
May leverage cached_l2norms if previously synchronized via sync_l2norms().

functions.name: faiss::IndexFlatL2::sync_l2norms
functions.signature: void faiss::IndexFlatL2::sync_l2norms();
functions.description: Computes and caches L2 norms of stored vectors to accelerate L2 distance computations.
requirements: The index must contain the vectors to compute norms for; call after additions or modifications to ensure the cache matches current data.
Recompute after any operation that changes stored vectors or order.

functions.name: faiss::IndexFlatL2::clear_l2norms
functions.signature: void faiss::IndexFlatL2::clear_l2norms();
functions.description: Clears the cached L2 norms, reverting to standard L2 computations without the cache.
requirements: Safe to call at any time; subsequent searches won’t use cached norms until sync_l2norms() is called again.

functions.name: faiss::IndexFlatPanorama::IndexFlatPanorama
functions.signature: explicit faiss::IndexFlatPanorama::IndexFlatPanorama(idx_t d, MetricType metric, size_t n_levels, size_t batch_size);
functions.description: Constructs a flat index with Panorama-based storage/acceleration layers. Supports batched organization across n_levels with given batch_size. Only L2 metric is supported and enforced.
requirements: d must be the vector dimensionality.
metric must be METRIC_L2; otherwise the constructor throws (FAISS_THROW_IF_NOT).
n_levels must be >= 1.
batch_size must be >= 1.
Index is empty after construction; add vectors before searching.

functions.name: faiss::IndexFlatPanorama::add
functions.signature: void faiss::IndexFlatPanorama::add(idx_t n, const float* x) override;
functions.description: Adds n vectors to the index and into the Panorama storage structure.
requirements: x must point to an array of size n * d floats.
n may be zero to add nothing.
Pointer x must be non-null unless n == 0.
Dimensionality of x rows must equal d.
Appends to existing data; IDs assigned sequentially starting at previous ntotal.

functions.name: faiss::IndexFlatPanorama::search
functions.signature: void faiss::IndexFlatPanorama::search(idx_t n, const float* x, idx_t k, float* distances, idx_t* labels, const SearchParameters* params = nullptr) const override;
functions.description: Performs exhaustive k-NN search using the Panorama-organized storage to accelerate computations. Returns top-k distances and IDs for each query.
requirements: x must be an array of size n * d.
distances must be an array of size n * k.
labels must be an array of size n * k.
k must be >= 1; typically k <= ntotal for fully valid outputs.
params, if non-null, must be a valid SearchParameters for this index type.
Index must contain vectors prior to search. Pointers must be non-null unless n == 0.

functions.name: faiss::IndexFlatPanorama::range_search
functions.signature: void faiss::IndexFlatPanorama::range_search(idx_t n, const float* x, float radius, RangeSearchResult* result, const SearchParameters* params = nullptr) const override;
functions.description: Performs exhaustive range search using Panorama storage, returning all neighbors within the specified radius via the RangeSearchResult collector.
requirements: x must be of size n * d.
result must be a valid RangeSearchResult for n queries.
radius must be non-negative and interpreted under L2 metric.
params, if non-null, must be valid for this index type.
Pointers must be non-null unless n == 0 (result must still be valid).

functions.name: faiss::IndexFlatPanorama::search_subset
functions.signature: void faiss::IndexFlatPanorama::search_subset(idx_t n, const float* x, idx_t k_base, const idx_t* base_labels, idx_t k, float* distances, idx_t* labels) const override;
functions.description: Searches only a specified subset of base candidates per query. For each query, base_labels supplies k_base candidate IDs to evaluate; the function returns the top-k among those.
requirements: x must point to queries of size n * d.
base_labels must point to an array of size n * k_base containing candidate database IDs for each query.
distances must be an array of size n * k for output distances.
labels must be an array of size n * k for output IDs.
All IDs in base_labels must be valid (0 <= id < ntotal).
k_base must be >= 1; k must be >= 1 and typically k <= k_base.
Pointers must be non-null unless n == 0.

functions.name: faiss::IndexFlatPanorama::reset
functions.signature: void faiss::IndexFlatPanorama::reset() override;
functions.description: Clears the index, removing all stored vectors and Panorama data, resetting ntotal to zero.
requirements: After reset, previous pointers from get_xb and any cached structures become invalid.
Safe to call even if the index is already empty.

functions.name: faiss::IndexFlatPanorama::reconstruct
functions.signature: void faiss::IndexFlatPanorama::reconstruct(idx_t key, float* recons) const override;
functions.description: Reconstructs the stored vector for the given ID from Panorama storage into the output buffer.
requirements: key must be a valid ID (0 <= key < ntotal).
recons must be a buffer of size d.
Pointer must be non-null.

functions.name: faiss::IndexFlatPanorama::reconstruct_n
functions.signature: void faiss::IndexFlatPanorama::reconstruct_n(idx_t i, idx_t n, float* recons) const override;
functions.description: Reconstructs n consecutive stored vectors starting at ID i into the output buffer.
requirements: i must be a valid starting ID and i + n must be <= ntotal.
recons must point to a buffer of size n * d.
Pointer must be non-null unless n == 0.

functions.name: faiss::IndexFlatPanorama::remove_ids
functions.signature: size_t faiss::IndexFlatPanorama::remove_ids(const IDSelector& sel) override;
functions.description: Removes all database vectors whose IDs are selected by sel. Returns the number of removed vectors.
requirements: sel must be a valid IDSelector that can be called to test membership.
Index contents and ID mapping may change; subsequent IDs may be compacted or permuted depending on implementation.

functions.name: faiss::IndexFlatPanorama::merge_from
functions.signature: void faiss::IndexFlatPanorama::merge_from(Index& otherIndex, idx_t add_id) override;
functions.description: Merges vectors from another index into this one, offsetting imported IDs by add_id as needed. Intended to concatenate/merge compatible indices.
requirements: otherIndex must be compatible in type, dimensionality, and metric (IndexFlatPanorama with L2) to be merged.
add_id specifies the starting ID offset for imported vectors and should be >= 0.
After merge, otherIndex may be modified or emptied depending on implementation.

functions.name: faiss::IndexFlatPanorama::add_sa_codes
functions.signature: void faiss::IndexFlatPanorama::add_sa_codes(idx_t n, const uint8_t* codes_in, const idx_t* xids) override;
functions.description: Adds n pre-encoded codes and associated IDs into the index’s storage. For Panorama/Flat, codes are float bytes for each vector.
requirements: codes_in must point to at least n * code_size bytes (code_size == d * sizeof(float) for flat float codes).
