functions.signature: virtual void faiss::IndexBinary::reconstruct_n(faiss::idx_t i0, faiss::idx_t ni, uint8_t* recons) const
functions.description: Reconstructs ni vectors with IDs in the range [i0, i0 + ni - 1] into the output buffer. May not be defined for some indexes.
requirements: recons must point to at least ni * (d / 8) bytes.
i0 and ni must define a valid range of IDs present in the index; otherwise behavior is implementation-defined (unknown).
Function may not be supported by all indexes (as stated).

functions.name: faiss::IndexBinary::search_and_reconstruct
functions.signature: virtual void faiss::IndexBinary::search_and_reconstruct(faiss::idx_t n, const uint8_t* x, faiss::idx_t k, int32_t* distances, faiss::idx_t* labels, uint8_t* recons, const faiss::SearchParameters* params = nullptr) const
functions.description: Performs k-NN search and also outputs the reconstructed stored vectors (or approximations) corresponding to the results. Pads labels with -1 where fewer than k results exist.
requirements: If n > 0, x must point to at least n * (d / 8) bytes.
distances must point to at least n * k int32_t elements when k > 0.
labels must point to at least n * k faiss::idx_t elements when k > 0.
recons must point to at least n * k * (d / 8) bytes to store reconstructed binary codes (inferred from description and binary code size).
params may be nullptr or a valid pointer to search parameters (unknown specifics).
Index must be in a valid searchable state (e.g., trained if required) (inferred).

functions.name: faiss::IndexBinary::display
functions.signature: void faiss::IndexBinary::display() const
functions.description: Prints the actual class name and additional information about the index to stdout or logs.
requirements: No arguments; used for diagnostics. Output destination and format are unspecified (unknown).

functions.name: faiss::IndexBinary::merge_from
functions.signature: virtual void faiss::IndexBinary::merge_from(faiss::IndexBinary& otherIndex, faiss::idx_t add_id = 0)
functions.description: Moves entries from otherIndex into this index, emptying otherIndex on success. add_id is added to all moved IDs (e.g., to offset sequential IDs).
requirements: otherIndex must be compatible with this index; use check_compatible_for_merge or expect an exception (as stated).
add_id is added to all moved IDs; ensure no overflow or ID collision in the destination (inferred).
On success, otherIndex becomes empty (as stated).

functions.name: faiss::IndexBinary::check_compatible_for_merge
functions.signature: virtual void faiss::IndexBinary::check_compatible_for_merge(const faiss::IndexBinary& otherIndex) const
functions.description: Checks that two indexes are compatible (e.g., trained the same way and share the same parameters). Throws if incompatible.
requirements: otherIndex must refer to an IndexBinary intended to be merged into this one.
Caller should handle exceptions thrown on incompatibility (as stated).

functions.name: faiss::IndexBinary::sa_code_size
functions.signature: virtual size_t faiss::IndexBinary::sa_code_size() const
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of the codes accepted by add_sa_codes for this index.
requirements: No arguments. Return value must be used to size the codes buffer for add_sa_codes (inferred).

functions.name: faiss::IndexBinary::add_sa_codes
functions.signature: virtual void faiss::IndexBinary::add_sa_codes(faiss::idx_t n, const uint8_t* codes, const faiss::idx_t* xids)
functions.description: Adds n precomputed (standalone) codes to the index with the given IDs. Semantically similar to add_with_ids but expects already-encoded codes matching sa_code_size().
requirements: If n > 0, codes must point to at least n * sa_code_size() bytes.
xids must point to at least n elements (as implied by add_with_ids semantics).
Codes must match the format/size expected by this index, i.e., sa_code_size() (as stated/inferred).
Function support may depend on the concrete index implementation (unknown).

functions.name: faiss::IndexBinaryFlat::IndexBinaryFlat
functions.signature: faiss::IndexBinaryFlat::IndexBinaryFlat(faiss::idx_t d)
functions.description: Constructs a binary flat index with dimensionality d (in bits). Stores added binary vectors verbatim and performs exhaustive (brute-force) Hamming-distance search.
requirements: d is the binary dimensionality in bits; the per-vector storage size will be d/8 bytes.
Caller should ensure that d corresponds to the dimensionality of all vectors that will be added to this index.
Behavior if d is not a multiple of 8 is unknown (implementation-specific).

functions.name: faiss::IndexBinaryFlat::IndexBinaryFlat
functions.signature: faiss::IndexBinaryFlat::IndexBinaryFlat()
functions.description: Default-constructs an empty binary flat index. Dimensionality d is not set by this constructor in the provided header; behavior may depend on base class defaults or subsequent initialization.
requirements: Before adding or searching, the index dimensionality d must be well-defined; how to set d after default construction is not shown in this header.
Using add/search/reconstruct with an unset/invalid d leads to undefined behavior.

functions.name: faiss::IndexBinaryFlat::add
functions.signature: void faiss::IndexBinaryFlat::add(faiss::idx_t n, const uint8_t* x)
functions.description: Appends n binary vectors to the index. Vectors are stored contiguously and used for exhaustive search.
requirements: If n > 0, x must be a valid, non-null pointer to at least n * (d/8) bytes, where d is the index dimensionality in bits.
Each input vector must be exactly d bits (d/8 bytes) long; vectors are packed in memory back-to-back.
The index must have been constructed with the desired dimensionality before calling add.
n may be 0 to perform a no-op.

functions.name: faiss::IndexBinaryFlat::reset
functions.signature: void faiss::IndexBinaryFlat::reset()
functions.description: Removes all vectors from the index and resets the database to empty.
requirements: After reset, any previously stored ids become invalid.
May be called at any time; no arguments and no return value.

functions.name: faiss::IndexBinaryFlat::search
functions.signature: void faiss::IndexBinaryFlat::search(faiss::idx_t n, const uint8_t* x, faiss::idx_t k, int32_t* distances, faiss::idx_t* labels, const faiss::SearchParameters* params = nullptr) const
functions.description: Performs exhaustive k-NN search for n query binary vectors against the stored database using Hamming distance. Writes the top-k distances and corresponding labels for each query.
requirements: If n > 0, x must point to at least n * (d/8) bytes of query data, with each query vector packed consecutively.
k must be >= 0. If k == 0, outputs are not written.
distances must point to a buffer of at least n * k int32_t entries to store Hamming distances.
labels must point to a buffer of at least n * k entries of type faiss::idx_t to store ids of matching database vectors.
If the index is empty, labels are typically set to -1 and distances may be set to max values (exact behavior may depend on FAISS conventions).
params may be null; if provided, it must outlive the call. Unknown fields in params are implementation-specific.

functions.name: faiss::IndexBinaryFlat::range_search
functions.signature: void faiss::IndexBinaryFlat::range_search(faiss::idx_t n, const uint8_t* x, int radius, faiss::RangeSearchResult* result, const faiss::SearchParameters* params = nullptr) const
functions.description: Performs exhaustive range search for n query binary vectors, returning all database vectors within the given Hamming-distance radius for each query.
requirements: If n > 0, x must point to at least n * (d/8) bytes of query data, with each query vector packed consecutively.
radius is the maximum allowed Hamming distance; it should be non-negative. Behavior for negative values is undefined.
result must be a valid, non-null pointer to a RangeSearchResult object prepared to collect results for n queries.
params may be null; if provided, it must outlive the call. Unknown fields in params are implementation-specific.

functions.name: faiss::IndexBinaryFlat::reconstruct
functions.signature: void faiss::IndexBinaryFlat::reconstruct(faiss::idx_t key, uint8_t* recons) const
functions.description: Retrieves the stored binary vector corresponding to the given internal id (key) and writes it to the output buffer.
requirements: key must refer to an existing stored vector: 0 <= key < ntotal.
recons must be a valid, non-null pointer to a buffer of at least (d/8) bytes.
The index must contain at least one vector for any reconstruction to succeed.

functions.name: faiss::IndexBinaryFlat::remove_ids
functions.signature: size_t faiss::IndexBinaryFlat::remove_ids(const faiss::IDSelector& sel)
functions.description: Removes all database vectors whose ids are selected by sel. In this flat binary index, ids of remaining vectors are shifted; they are not preserved.
requirements: sel must be a valid selector that can be queried during the call.
Callers must not assume id stability: after removal, the ids of remaining vectors may change (are shifted).
Returns the number of removed vectors; callers should use this to validate the effect of the operation.

functions.name: faiss::IndexBinaryHNSW::IndexBinaryHNSW
functions.signature: explicit faiss::IndexBinaryHNSW::IndexBinaryHNSW();
functions.description: Default constructor for an HNSW-based binary index. Initializes an empty index with default HNSW parameters and internal storage. Intended for subsequent configuration and population via train/add.
requirements: May require setting dimension and/or attaching storage before use; exact defaults are unknown from this header.
Must call add() with valid data to populate before meaningful search; otherwise results are undefined/empty.
Thread-safety of construction and subsequent use is unknown.

functions.name: faiss::IndexBinaryHNSW::IndexBinaryHNSW
functions.signature: explicit faiss::IndexBinaryHNSW::IndexBinaryHNSW(int d, int M = 32);
functions.description: Constructs an HNSW-based binary index with dimensionality d (in bits) and HNSW connectivity parameter M. Prepares internal storage and HNSW graph for binary vectors of the specified dimension.
requirements: d must be a positive integer representing the number of bits in each binary vector.
M should be a positive integer; larger values increase graph connectivity and memory usage. Exact valid range is not specified here.
Vectors subsequently added must have size exactly d/8 bytes each.

functions.name: faiss::IndexBinaryHNSW::IndexBinaryHNSW
functions.signature: explicit faiss::IndexBinaryHNSW::IndexBinaryHNSW(faiss::IndexBinary* storage, int M = 32);
functions.description: Constructs an HNSW-based binary index that uses the provided IndexBinary storage for sequential data, with HNSW connectivity parameter M. Useful to wrap an existing binary storage backend with an HNSW graph.
requirements: storage must be a valid, non-null pointer to an IndexBinary compatible with the intended dimension.
The storage's dimension must match the vectors to be added; mismatch handling is unknown here.
M should be a positive integer; exact valid range is not specified.
Ownership semantics of storage are controlled by own_fields in this class; specific rules are not documented in this header.

functions.name: faiss::IndexBinaryHNSW::~IndexBinaryHNSW
functions.signature: faiss::IndexBinaryHNSW::~IndexBinaryHNSW() override;
functions.description: Destructor for the HNSW-based binary index. Releases resources associated with the HNSW graph and any owned storage.
requirements: After destruction, all pointers previously returned by the index (if any) must no longer be used.
Ownership and lifetime of external storage when own_fields is false are not defined here.

functions.name: faiss::IndexBinaryHNSW::get_distance_computer
functions.signature: faiss::DistanceComputer* faiss::IndexBinaryHNSW::get_distance_computer() const;
functions.description: Returns a DistanceComputer instance suitable for computing distances consistent with this index’s metric on binary vectors. Typically used internally or by advanced callers for custom search routines.
requirements: Must be called on a properly initialized index (dimension and metric must be set).
Returned pointer must be treated according to FAISS ownership conventions; ownership and deletion responsibility are not specified in this header (unknown).
Thread-safety of using the returned object concurrently is unknown.

functions.name: faiss::IndexBinaryHNSW::add
functions.signature: void faiss::IndexBinaryHNSW::add(idx_t n, const uint8_t* x) override;
functions.description: Adds n binary vectors to the index and updates the HNSW graph structure. Each vector is d bits long (d/8 bytes).
requirements: If n > 0, x must be a valid pointer to at least n * (d/8) bytes of memory, with vectors laid out contiguously.
The index must have been constructed/trained such that its dimensionality d is defined, and the input vectors must match this dimension.
Behavior when adding while base-level initialization flags (init_level0/keep_max_size_level0) are toggled is internal; no special caller action required here.
May be expensive; no guaranteed thread-safety for concurrent add() calls unless externally synchronized.

functions.name: faiss::IndexBinaryHNSW::train
functions.signature: void faiss::IndexBinaryHNSW::train(idx_t n, const uint8_t* x) override;
functions.description: Trains the underlying storage if needed using n training vectors. For flat binary storage, training is typically a no-op, but other storage backends may require it.
requirements: If training is required and n > 0, x must point to at least n * (d/8) bytes of contiguous data.
Must be called before add() if the chosen storage backend requires training; whether training is required depends on the storage and is not specified here.
n may be 0 if no training data is needed; exact behavior with n=0 is unspecified.

functions.name: faiss::IndexBinaryHNSW::search
functions.signature: void faiss::IndexBinaryHNSW::search(idx_t n, const uint8_t* x, idx_t k, int32_t* distances, idx_t* labels, const faiss::SearchParameters* params = nullptr) const override;
functions.description: Performs approximate nearest neighbor search on n query binary vectors, returning the top-k results per query according to the index’s distance (typically Hamming distance). Results are written to distances (int32) and labels (idx_t).
requirements: If n > 0, x must point to at least n * (d/8) bytes of contiguous query data.
k must be a positive integer; distances and labels must each have capacity for n * k elements.
distances must be a valid pointer to int32_t and labels to idx_t; buffers must be writable.
params may be nullptr; when provided, it must point to a valid SearchParameters object compatible with this index.
Index must be built/populated (ntotal >= 0); searching an empty index yields implementation-defined results (often -1 labels).

functions.name: faiss::IndexBinaryHNSW::reconstruct
functions.signature: void faiss::IndexBinaryHNSW::reconstruct(idx_t key, uint8_t* recons) const override;
functions.description: Reconstructs the binary vector corresponding to the given key (label/id) and writes it to recons.
requirements: key must refer to a valid vector in the index; typically 0 <= key < ntotal.
recons must point to a buffer of at least d/8 bytes.
Behavior for invalid keys is unspecified here and may raise an error or leave recons undefined.

functions.name: faiss::IndexBinaryHNSW::reset
functions.signature: void faiss::IndexBinaryHNSW::reset() override;
functions.description: Clears the index contents and HNSW graph, resetting it to an empty state while preserving configuration parameters.
requirements: All previously returned labels become invalid after reset.
Subsequent searches on an empty index will not return meaningful results until new data is added.

functions.name: faiss::IndexBinaryHNSWCagra::IndexBinaryHNSWCagra
functions.signature: faiss::IndexBinaryHNSWCagra::IndexBinaryHNSWCagra();
functions.description: Default constructor for the CAGRA-compatible HNSW binary index variant. Can operate in a base-level-only mode to interoperate with GPU-built graphs.
requirements: If base_level_only is set to true by the caller, the index becomes immutable for additions (see add requirements).
Other initialization details (dimension, storage) follow the base class; specifics are not provided here.

functions.name: faiss::IndexBinaryHNSWCagra::IndexBinaryHNSWCagra
functions.signature: faiss::IndexBinaryHNSWCagra::IndexBinaryHNSWCagra(int d, int M);
functions.description: Constructs a CAGRA-compatible HNSW binary index of dimensionality d (bits) with connectivity parameter M.
requirements: d must be a positive integer representing the number of bits per vector.
M should be a positive integer; exact valid range is not specified here.
Vectors subsequently added must have size exactly d/8 bytes each.

functions.name: faiss::IndexBinaryHNSWCagra::add
functions.signature: void faiss::IndexBinaryHNSWCagra::add(idx_t n, const uint8_t* x) override;
functions.description: Adds n binary vectors to the CAGRA-compatible HNSW index. In base-level-only mode, additions are disabled to preserve the GPU-copied base graph.
requirements: If n > 0, x must be a valid pointer to at least n * (d/8) bytes of contiguous data.
Index dimensionality d must match the input vectors.
If base_level_only is true, do not call add(); additions are not allowed in this mode.
Thread-safety for concurrent add() is not guaranteed.

functions.name: faiss::IndexBinaryHNSWCagra::search
functions.signature: void faiss::IndexBinaryHNSWCagra::search(idx_t n, const uint8_t* x, idx_t k, int32_t* distances, idx_t* labels, const faiss::SearchParameters* params = nullptr) const override;
functions.description: Performs approximate nearest neighbor search on n query vectors. When base_level_only is true, the search is restricted to the base-level KNN graph using a randomized selection of entry points controlled by num_base_level_search_entrypoints.
requirements: If n > 0, x must point to at least n * (d/8) bytes of contiguous query data.
k must be positive; distances and labels must each have capacity for n * k elements.
distances must be int32_t* and labels idx_t*, both writable.
params may be nullptr or point to a valid SearchParameters instance.
Behavior and performance depend on base_level_only and num_base_level_search_entrypoints; functional correctness does not require caller action beyond providing valid inputs.

functions.name: faiss::IndexRowwiseMinMaxBase::IndexRowwiseMinMaxBase
functions.signature: faiss::IndexRowwiseMinMaxBase::IndexRowwiseMinMaxBase(faiss::Index* index)
functions.description: Constructs a rowwise min-max normalization wrapper around a provided sub-index. The wrapper will normalize each input vector row to [0,1] (preserving coefficients) before delegating to the sub-index’s train/encode paths and store per-row scaling factors alongside encoded data.
requirements: index must be a valid faiss::Index pointer that remains alive for the lifetime of this wrapper, unless the wrapper takes ownership (own_fields) internally.

The provided sub-index must be compatible with vector-codec operations expected by this wrapper (i.e., support training/adding/searching; derived classes use subindex::train and subindex::sa_encode/sa_decode).
Callers should ensure the sub-index dimensionality matches the vectors that will be provided to this wrapper (d must match).

functions.name: faiss::IndexRowwiseMinMaxBase::IndexRowwiseMinMaxBase
functions.signature: faiss::IndexRowwiseMinMaxBase::IndexRowwiseMinMaxBase()
functions.description: Default constructor for the rowwise min-max normalization wrapper. No sub-index is provided at construction time. Intended for scenarios like deserialization; behavior until a valid sub-index is associated is unspecified in this header.
requirements: Before calling train/add/search or codec methods on a default-constructed instance, a valid compatible sub-index must be set/available; otherwise, operations will fail. The mechanism to set the sub-index is not defined in this header (unknown; likely via deserialization).
Vector dimensionality d must be set consistently with the eventual sub-index before usage.

functions.name: faiss::IndexRowwiseMinMaxBase::~IndexRowwiseMinMaxBase
functions.signature: faiss::IndexRowwiseMinMaxBase::~IndexRowwiseMinMaxBase() override
functions.description: Destructor for the rowwise min-max normalization wrapper. If the wrapper owns its sub-index (own_fields), it will free it; otherwise, it leaves the sub-index unmanaged.
requirements: After destruction, the object and any owned sub-index must no longer be accessed by callers.
Ownership semantics (own_fields) determine whether the sub-index is released; callers must not double-free externally owned sub-indexes.

functions.name: faiss::IndexRowwiseMinMaxBase::add
functions.signature: void faiss::IndexRowwiseMinMaxBase::add(faiss::idx_t n, const float* x) override
functions.description: Adds n vectors to the index after applying rowwise min-max normalization to [0,1], delegating storage/encoding to the sub-index. The wrapper preserves per-row scaling coefficients in the encoded representation used by derived classes.
requirements: x must point to a contiguous array of n * d float values, where d == this->d.
If n == 0, x may be null; otherwise x must be non-null.
The underlying sub-index must be in a state that allows adding (e.g., trained if required by the sub-index).
The instance must have a valid compatible sub-index associated before calling add.

functions.name: faiss::IndexRowwiseMinMaxBase::search
functions.signature: void faiss::IndexRowwiseMinMaxBase::search(faiss::idx_t n, const float* x, faiss::idx_t k, float* distances, faiss::idx_t* labels, const faiss::SearchParameters* params = nullptr) const override
functions.description: Searches the index for the k nearest neighbors of n query vectors. Each query vector is rowwise normalized to [0,1] before delegating to the sub-index search. Returns distances and labels for each query.
requirements: x must point to a contiguous array of n * d float values; d == this->d.
distances must point to a contiguous array of size n * k (non-null if n > 0 and k > 0).
labels must point to a contiguous array of size n * k (non-null if n > 0 and k > 0).
k must be >= 1 for meaningful results; behavior for k == 0 is sub-index defined (avoid).
params may be null; if provided, it must be a valid pointer to a faiss::SearchParameters compatible with the sub-index.
The index must be populated and any required training completed prior to search.
A valid compatible sub-index must be associated with this wrapper before calling search.

functions.name: faiss::IndexRowwiseMinMaxBase::reset
functions.signature: void faiss::IndexRowwiseMinMaxBase::reset() override
functions.description: Clears all indexed data, resetting the index to an empty state while preserving the index configuration. Applies to the wrapped sub-index.
requirements: After reset, previously added data are no longer available for search.
A valid compatible sub-index must be associated; otherwise reset may be a no-op or error (unspecified in header).

functions.name: faiss::IndexRowwiseMinMaxBase::train_inplace
functions.signature: virtual void faiss::IndexRowwiseMinMaxBase::train_inplace(faiss::idx_t n, float* x) = 0
functions.description: Trains the underlying sub-index using input data that are scaled in-place to [0,1] rowwise, then (implicitly) scaled back. This avoids cloning the dataset but modifies the caller’s buffer during the operation. Implemented by derived classes.
requirements: x must point to a mutable contiguous array of n * d float values; d == this->d.
The buffer x will be modified during training; callers must allow this and not assume x remains unchanged while training executes.
n may be 0; if n > 0, x must be non-null.
A valid compatible sub-index must exist before calling train_inplace.
Call only when it is acceptable for the training data buffer to be mutated temporarily.

functions.name: faiss::IndexRowwiseMinMaxFP16::IndexRowwiseMinMaxFP16
functions.signature: faiss::IndexRowwiseMinMaxFP16::IndexRowwiseMinMaxFP16(faiss::Index* index)
functions.description: Constructs a rowwise min-max wrapper that stores per-row scaling coefficients as fp16 in the encoded representation. Uses the given sub-index for storage/search.
requirements: index must be a valid faiss::Index pointer compatible with vector codec operations expected by this wrapper (train, sa_encode, sa_decode).
The sub-index dimensionality must match the vectors’ dimension d.
The sub-index must outlive this wrapper unless ownership is transferred internally.

functions.name: faiss::IndexRowwiseMinMaxFP16::IndexRowwiseMinMaxFP16
functions.signature: faiss::IndexRowwiseMinMaxFP16::IndexRowwiseMinMaxFP16()
functions.description: Default constructor for the fp16-coefficient rowwise min-max wrapper. No sub-index is provided. Typically used for deserialization; use is undefined until a valid sub-index is associated.
requirements: Before calling any operation (train/add/search/encode/decode), ensure a valid compatible sub-index is associated with the instance.
Ensure d is set consistently with the eventual sub-index before use.

functions.name: faiss::IndexRowwiseMinMaxFP16::train
functions.signature: void faiss::IndexRowwiseMinMaxFP16::train(faiss::idx_t n, const float* x) override
functions.description: Trains the underlying sub-index using data that are first rowwise scaled to [0,1] (non-inplace). The wrapper handles scaling and delegates to subindex::train. Scaling coefficients are not stored during training.
requirements: x must point to a contiguous array of n * d float values; d == this->d.
If n == 0, x may be null; otherwise x must be non-null.
A valid compatible sub-index must be associated prior to training.
Sufficient memory must be available for any temporary buffers used during scaling (implementation-defined).

functions.name: faiss::IndexRowwiseMinMaxFP16::train_inplace
functions.signature: void faiss::IndexRowwiseMinMaxFP16::train_inplace(faiss::idx_t n, float* x) override
functions.description: Trains the sub-index using in-place rowwise scaling of the training data to [0,1], avoiding cloning but temporarily modifying the input buffer. After training, data are scaled back.

template <typename IndexT>
void faiss::IndexShardsTemplate<IndexT>::add_shard(IndexT* index)
functions.description: Adds a sub-index (shard) to the composite index. This is an alias for addIndex() from ThreadedIndex and registers the shard so that future train/add/search calls are distributed over it.
requirements: index must be a valid, initialized IndexT pointer.
The shard's vector dimension must match the sharded index's dimension (or define it if it is the first shard when no explicit dimension was set).
The shard must be compatible with distributed operations of this class (e.g., support for add/add_with_ids/search as used).
Ownership/lifetime of index is unspecified in this header; the caller must ensure it remains valid for the lifetime of the sharded index or until remove_shard is called.

void faiss::IndexShardsTemplate<IndexT>::remove_shard(IndexT* index)

functions.name: faiss::IndexShardsTemplate::add
functions.signature:
template <typename IndexT>
void faiss::IndexShardsTemplate<IndexT>::add(faiss::idx_t n, const typename IndexT::component_t* x)
functions.description: Adds n vectors to the index, distributing them across shards. Supported only when sub-indices implement add_with_ids; otherwise, addition may not be possible. When successive_ids is true and ids are not supplied, ids will be shifted per-shard based on shard sizes.
requirements: n must be non-negative; if n > 0, x must point to at least n * d components where d is the vector dimension.
Sub-indices must implement add_with_ids (as stated) for this to function correctly.
All shards must share the same dimension as this index.
Behavior regarding id assignment follows the class’s successive_ids policy; explicit id control is available via add_with_ids.

functions.name: faiss::IndexShardsTemplate::add_with_ids
functions.signature:
template <typename IndexT>
void faiss::IndexShardsTemplate<IndexT>::add_with_ids(faiss::idx_t n, const typename IndexT::component_t* x, const faiss::idx_t* xids)
functions.description: Adds n vectors with caller-specified ids, distributing them across shards. Id shifting and distribution follow the documented cases for successive_ids and xids. This method coordinates add/add_with_ids calls to the shards based on inputs.
requirements: n must be non-negative; if n > 0, x must point to at least n * d components where d is the vector dimension.
If successive_ids == true and xids != NULL: ERROR/unsupported per comment; do not call with both set (it makes no sense to pass ids and request shifting).
If successive_ids == true and xids == NULL: allowed; should be called only once, and it will call add() on sub-indices (implicit id assignment).
If successive_ids == false and xids != NULL: allowed; will call add_with_ids on shards, distributing the provided ids evenly over shards.
If successive_ids == false and xids == NULL: allowed; will call add_with_ids on each sub-index, starting at ntotal (ids assigned starting from current total).
All shards must share the same dimension as this index.
x and xids (when non-NULL) must reference valid, readable memory for n vectors and n ids, respectively.

functions.name: faiss::IndexPQ::sa_decode
functions.signature: void faiss::IndexPQ::sa_decode(faiss::idx_t n, const uint8_t* bytes, float* x) const
functions.description: Decodes n PQ codes from bytes back into approximate reconstructed vectors x of dimension d each. Standalone codec interface corresponding to sa_encode.
requirements: bytes must point to n * code_size bytes, where code_size is the PQ code size used by this index.
x must point to writable memory for n*d floats.
The PQ (pq) must be trained and consistent with the codes being decoded.

functions.name: faiss::IndexPQ::get_FlatCodesDistanceComputer
functions.signature: faiss::FlatCodesDistanceComputer* faiss::IndexPQ::get_FlatCodesDistanceComputer() const
functions.description: Returns a distance-computer object specialized for computing distances between queries and flat PQ codes stored by this index. Intended for internal/advanced use to iterate over codes and compute distances efficiently.
requirements: Return pointer remains valid as per IndexFlatCodes policy (lifetime tied to the index or to the created object; exact ownership semantics unknown).
Caller must handle the returned pointer according to FAISS ownership rules (may need to delete or not; unknown).

functions.name: faiss::IndexPQ::search_core_polysemous
functions.signature: void faiss::IndexPQ::search_core_polysemous(faiss::idx_t n, const float* x, faiss::idx_t k, float* distances, faiss::idx_t* labels, int polysemous_ht, bool generalized_hamming) const
functions.description: Performs the core polysemous search: applies a Hamming-distance-based filter on PQ codes with threshold polysemous_ht (generalized if requested), then combines with PQ distance to produce k nearest neighbors for each query. Used internally when polysemous search is selected.
requirements: x must point to n*d floats stored contiguously.
k must be >= 1.
distances must point to writable memory of size n*k.
labels must point to writable memory of size n*k.
polysemous_ht is the Hamming threshold used for filtering; must be >= 0 and typically <= (M*nbits) (implied by histogram range).
The index must be trained and populated with codes.

functions.name: faiss::IndexPQ::hamming_distance_histogram
functions.signature: void faiss::IndexPQ::hamming_distance_histogram(faiss::idx_t n, const float* x, faiss::idx_t nb, const float* xb, int64_t* dist_histogram)
functions.description: Prepares queries for a polysemous search and computes the histogram of Hamming distances between encoded queries and codes. If xb is provided, computes against the provided dataset; otherwise uses the index’s stored codes. The histogram has bins from 0 to M*nbits inclusive.
requirements: x must point to n*d floats stored contiguously.
If xb is non-null, it must point to nb*d floats; if xb is null, nb is ignored and the index’s database is used.
dist_histogram must point to writable memory of length (M * nbits + 1) int64_t values.
The PQ must be trained; if xb is null, the index must contain database codes.

functions.name: faiss::IndexPQ::hamming_distance_table
functions.signature: void faiss::IndexPQ::hamming_distance_table(faiss::idx_t n, const float* x, int32_t* dis) const
functions.description: Computes pairwise Hamming distances between n query vectors (after PQ encoding) and the database codes, writing an n-by-ntotal distance table (row-major).
requirements: x must point to n*d floats stored contiguously.
dis must point to writable memory of size n * ntotal int32_t values, where ntotal is the number of indexed codes.
The PQ must be trained and the index must contain database codes.

functions.name: faiss::IndexPQStats::IndexPQStats
functions.signature: faiss::IndexPQStats::IndexPQStats()
functions.description: Constructs statistics container for IndexPQ queries and code visits. Initializes counters to zero via reset(). Safe for internal threading but not for concurrent calls to IndexPQ::search from multiple threads.
requirements: No special requirements; constructed object is ready to use.
Statistics are not thread-safe if multiple threads call IndexPQ::search concurrently.

functions.name: faiss::IndexPQStats::reset
functions.signature: void faiss::IndexPQStats::reset()
functions.description: Resets all collected statistics (nq, ncode, n_hamming_pass) to zero.
requirements: Object must be a valid IndexPQStats instance.

functions.name: faiss::MultiIndexQuantizer::MultiIndexQuantizer
functions.signature: faiss::MultiIndexQuantizer::MultiIndexQuantizer(int d, size_t M, size_t nbits)
functions.description: Constructs a MultiIndexQuantizer whose centroids are formed as the Cartesian product of sub-centroids from a ProductQuantizer with M subquantizers and nbits bits each for d-dimensional inputs. Used as a quantizer (no storage of database vectors).
requirements: d must be a positive integer (input dimensionality).
M must be a positive integer (number of subquantizers).
nbits must be a positive integer (bits per subvector index).
Must be trained on data before meaningful search/assignment.

functions.name: faiss::MultiIndexQuantizer::MultiIndexQuantizer
functions.signature: faiss::MultiIndexQuantizer::MultiIndexQuantizer()
functions.description: Default constructor for an uninitialized MultiIndexQuantizer. Typically used for deserialization; must be configured and trained before use.
requirements: Object is not ready for use until its parameters (d, M, nbits) are set and it is trained.

functions.name: faiss::MultiIndexQuantizer::train
functions.signature: void faiss::MultiIndexQuantizer::train(faiss::idx_t n, const float* x)
functions.description: Trains the internal ProductQuantizer on n training vectors x of dimension d so that assignments (cartesian-product centroids) can be computed.
requirements: x must point to n*d floats stored contiguously.
n must be >= 0 and sufficiently large for PQ training (exact minimum unknown).
The instance dimensionality d must match the vectors provided.

functions.name: faiss::MultiIndexQuantizer::search
functions.signature: void faiss::MultiIndexQuantizer::search(faiss::idx_t n, const float* x, faiss::idx_t k, float* distances, faiss::idx_t* labels, const faiss::SearchParameters* params = nullptr) const
functions.description: Assigns each of the n query vectors x to the k closest Cartesian-product centroids and returns their distances and labels. Acts as a quantizer; does not add or store vectors.
requirements: x must point to n*d floats stored contiguously.
k must be >= 1.
distances must point to writable memory of size n*k.
labels must point to writable memory of size n*k.
The quantizer must be trained before search.
params, if provided, must be valid for the duration of the call.

functions.name: faiss::MultiIndexQuantizer::add
functions.signature: void faiss::MultiIndexQuantizer::add(faiss::idx_t n, const float* x)
functions.description: Intentionally unsupported in MultiIndexQuantizer: calling add will crash at runtime. MultiIndexQuantizer is a quantizer (no database storage), not an index of stored vectors.
requirements: Do not call this function; it will crash at runtime as per the header comment.

functions.name: faiss::MultiIndexQuantizer::reset
functions.signature: void faiss::MultiIndexQuantizer::reset()
functions.description: Intentionally unsupported in MultiIndexQuantizer: calling reset will crash at runtime. MultiIndexQuantizer does not manage stored vectors.
requirements: Do not call this function; it will crash at runtime as per the header comment.

functions.name: faiss::MultiIndexQuantizer::reconstruct
functions.signature: void faiss::MultiIndexQuantizer::reconstruct(faiss::idx_t key, float* recons) const
functions.description: Reconstructs the centroid vector corresponding to a cartesian-product centroid index key into recons (length d).
requirements: key must be a valid centroid label within the range of possible PQ cartesian-product codes (exact range depends on M and nbits).
recons must point to writable memory for d floats.
The quantizer must be trained so that centroids exist.

functions.name: faiss::MultiIndexQuantizer2::MultiIndexQuantizer2
functions.signature: faiss::MultiIndexQuantizer2::MultiIndexQuantizer2(int d, size_t M, size_t nbits, faiss::Index** indexes)
functions.description: Constructs a MultiIndexQuantizer2 that performs the PQ assignment using M provided sub-indexes operating on d/M dimensions each. The sub-index array supplies the assignment mechanism per subquantizer.
requirements: d must be divisible by M so that each sub-index can operate on d/M dimensions (implied by design; exact enforcement unknown).
M must be a positive integer matching the number of provided indexes.
indexes must point to an array of M valid faiss::Index* covering the subspaces.
nbits must be a positive integer (bits per subvector index).
The quantizer must be trained before searching.

functions.name: faiss::MultiIndexQuantizer2::MultiIndexQuantizer2
functions.signature: faiss::MultiIndexQuantizer2::MultiIndexQuantizer2(int d, size_t nbits, faiss::Index* assign_index_0, faiss::Index* assign_index_1)
functions.description: Constructs a 2-subquantizer MultiIndexQuantizer2 using two provided sub-indexes that operate on d/2 dimensions each, with nbits bits per subvector index.
requirements: d must be divisible by 2 so that each sub-index can operate on d/2 dimensions (implied by design; exact enforcement unknown).
assign_index_0 and assign_index_1 must be valid faiss::Index* covering complementary subspaces.
nbits must be a positive integer (bits per subvector index).
The quantizer must be trained before searching.

functions.name: faiss::MultiIndexQuantizer2::train
functions.signature: void faiss::MultiIndexQuantizer2::train(faiss::idx_t n, const float* x)
functions.description: Trains the MultiIndexQuantizer2 using the provided training vectors. Training may involve training underlying sub-indexes or the internal PQ so that assignments can be performed.
requirements: x must point to n*d floats stored contiguously.
n must be >= 0 and sufficiently large for training (exact minimum unknown).
All sub-indexes (if owned/used) must be compatible with the subspace dimensionalities.

functions.name: faiss::MultiIndexQuantizer2::search
functions.signature: void faiss::MultiIndexQuantizer2::search(faiss::idx_t n, const float* x, faiss::idx_t k, float* distances, faiss::idx_t* labels, const faiss::SearchParameters* params = nullptr) const
functions.description: Assigns each of the n query vectors x to the k closest cartesian-product centroids using sub-index-based assignments and returns distances and labels.
requirements: x must point to n*d floats stored contiguously.
k must be >= 1.
distances must point to writable memory of size n*k.
labels must point to writable memory of size n*k.
The quantizer must be trained before search.
params, if provided, must be valid for the duration of the call.

functions.name: faiss::IndexPreTransform::IndexPreTransform
functions.signature: faiss::IndexPreTransform::IndexPreTransform(faiss::Index* index)
functions.description: Constructs an IndexPreTransform that forwards operations to the provided sub-index after applying any configured transform chain. The sub-index pointer is stored; this constructor does not itself add transforms.
requirements: index must point to a valid faiss::Index instance whose lifetime outlives or is managed by this IndexPreTransform unless own_fields is set to take ownership (ownership semantics are not specified here).
index must be compatible with any transforms later added so that vector dimensionalities match.

functions.name: faiss::IndexPreTransform::IndexPreTransform
functions.signature: faiss::IndexPreTransform::IndexPreTransform()
functions.description: Default-constructs an empty IndexPreTransform. The transform chain and sub-index can be configured later before use.
requirements: Before calling train/add/search functions, a valid sub-index must be installed (e.g., via constructor or other configuration path); otherwise behavior is undefined or will fail.
Transform chain and sub-index must be dimensionally consistent before training or adding vectors.

functions.name: faiss::IndexPreTransform::IndexPreTransform
functions.signature: faiss::IndexPreTransform::IndexPreTransform(faiss::VectorTransform* ltrans, faiss::Index* index)
functions.description: Constructs an IndexPreTransform with an initial transform (applied last before the index) and a sub-index. Additional transforms can be prepended later.
requirements: ltrans must point to a valid faiss::VectorTransform instance compatible with the sub-index input dimensionality.
index must point to a valid faiss::Index instance with input dimensionality equal to ltrans output dimensionality.
Ownership/cleanup of ltrans and index depends on own_fields; specific ownership semantics are not specified here.

functions.name: faiss::IndexPreTransform::prepend_transform
functions.signature: void faiss::IndexPreTransform::prepend_transform(faiss::VectorTransform* ltrans)
functions.description: Prepends a VectorTransform to the transform chain so it is applied before existing transforms and the sub-index during all subsequent operations.
requirements: ltrans must be a valid, initialized faiss::VectorTransform.
The output dimensionality of ltrans must match the input dimensionality expected by the next element in the chain (or the sub-index if the chain was empty).
The transform chain must remain dimensionally consistent after insertion.

functions.name: faiss::IndexPreTransform::train
functions.signature: void faiss::IndexPreTransform::train(faiss::idx_t n, const float* x)
functions.description: Trains the underlying transforms/index using n training vectors after applying the transform chain to x. Delegates to sub-components that require training.
requirements: If n > 0, x must point to at least n contiguous input vectors in the original feature space with the expected dimensionality d.
The sub-index and all transforms that require training must be properly configured and dimensionally consistent prior to calling.
If the index or transforms are already trained, retraining behavior depends on their implementations (unspecified here).

functions.name: faiss::IndexPreTransform::add
functions.signature: void faiss::IndexPreTransform::add(faiss::idx_t n, const float* x)
functions.description: Adds n vectors to the index after applying the transform chain. New vectors receive auto-assigned ids by the sub-index.
requirements: If n > 0, x must point to at least n contiguous input vectors with the expected dimensionality d.
Index and transforms must be trained if required by their implementations before adding.
Sufficient capacity/memory must be available in the sub-index to store n vectors.

functions.name: faiss::IndexPreTransform::add_with_ids
functions.signature: void faiss::IndexPreTransform::add_with_ids(faiss::idx_t n, const float* x, const faiss::idx_t* xids)
functions.description: Adds n vectors with caller-specified ids after applying the transform chain. Delegates to the sub-index with the provided ids.
requirements: If n > 0, x must point to at least n input vectors and xids must point to at least n ids.
Each id in xids must satisfy the sub-index's id constraints (e.g., uniqueness); exact rules depend on the sub-index.
Index and transforms must be trained if required before adding.

functions.name: faiss::IndexPreTransform::reset
functions.signature: void faiss::IndexPreTransform::reset()
functions.description: Clears the contents of the sub-index (and any cached state) while keeping the index structure and transforms intact.
requirements: The sub-index must support reset; semantics are those of the underlying index.
After reset, previously added vectors and ids are removed.

functions.name: faiss::IndexPreTransform::remove_ids
functions.signature: size_t faiss::IndexPreTransform::remove_ids(const faiss::IDSelector& sel)
functions.description: Removes vectors whose ids are selected by sel from the sub-index. Not supported by all sub-index types.
requirements: The sub-index must support id removal; otherwise this may be a no-op or raise an error depending on implementation.
sel must remain valid for the duration of the call.
Caller should handle the case where zero ids are removed.

functions.name: faiss::IndexPreTransform::search
functions.signature: void faiss::IndexPreTransform::search(faiss::idx_t n, const float* x, faiss::idx_t k, float* distances, faiss::idx_t* labels, const faiss::SearchParameters* params = nullptr) const
functions.description: Searches the index for the top-k nearest neighbors of n query vectors after applying the transform chain. Results are written to distances and labels. Optional search parameters can be provided and may be wrapped in SearchParametersPreTransform to forward sub-index parameters.
requirements: If n > 0, x must point to at least n query vectors with the expected input dimensionality.
distances must have capacity for n * k floats; labels must have capacity for n * k ids.
k must be >= 1 and supported by the sub-index.
params, if provided, must be compatible with this index; when using SearchParametersPreTransform, its index_params can point to parameters for the sub-index.

functions.name: faiss::IndexPreTransform::search_subset
functions.signature: void faiss::IndexPreTransform::search_subset(faiss::idx_t n, const float* x, faiss::idx_t k_base, const faiss::idx_t* base_labels, faiss::idx_t k, float* distances, faiss::idx_t* labels) const
functions.description: Performs search restricted to a provided base candidate set specified via base_labels for each query, after applying the transform chain. Returns the top-k results per query within the subset.
requirements: If n > 0, x must point to at least n query vectors.
base_labels must provide at least n * k_base candidate ids (layout and validity as required by the sub-index).
distances and labels must each have capacity for n * k results.
k_base must be >= 0; k must be >= 1; both must be consistent with buffer sizes.
All candidate ids in base_labels must be valid in the sub-index.

functions.name: faiss::IndexPreTransform::range_search
functions.signature: void faiss::IndexPreTransform::range_search(faiss::idx_t n, const float* x, float radius, faiss::RangeSearchResult* result, const faiss::SearchParameters* params = nullptr) const
functions.description: Performs range search for n queries after applying the transform chain, retrieving all neighbors within the given radius in the sub-index. The search radius is not adjusted by the transforms.
requirements: If n > 0, x must point to at least n query vectors.
result must be a valid, initialized RangeSearchResult to collect outputs.
radius must be non-negative and interpreted by the sub-index's metric.
params, if provided, must be compatible with this index; SearchParametersPreTransform can be used to forward sub-index parameters.

functions.name: faiss::IndexPreTransform::reconstruct
functions.signature: void faiss::IndexPreTransform::reconstruct(faiss::idx_t key, float* recons) const
functions.description: Reconstructs the original-space vector for the given id by obtaining the sub-index’s representation and reversing the transform chain as supported.
requirements: key must be a valid id present in the sub-index.
recons must point to a buffer large enough to hold one reconstructed vector in the original input dimensionality.
Reverse reconstruction may be approximate or unsupported for some transforms; behavior depends on the chain.

functions.name: faiss::IndexPreTransform::reconstruct_n
functions.signature: void faiss::IndexPreTransform::reconstruct_n(faiss::idx_t i0, faiss::idx_t ni, float* recons) const
functions.description: Reconstructs ni consecutive vectors with ids in [i0, i0+ni) into the original space by reversing the transform chain as supported.
requirements: recons must have capacity for ni vectors in the original input dimensionality.
All ids in the range [i0, i0+ni) must be valid in the sub-index; unsupported ids may cause errors depending on the implementation.
Reverse reconstruction support and accuracy depend on the transforms.

functions.name: faiss::IndexPreTransform::search_and_reconstruct
functions.signature: void faiss::IndexPreTransform::search_and_reconstruct(faiss::idx_t n, const float* x, faiss::idx_t k, float* distances, faiss::idx_t* labels, float* recons, const faiss::SearchParameters* params = nullptr) const
functions.description: Searches for top-k nearest neighbors for n queries after applying the transform chain, and also reconstructs the found vectors back into the original space where supported, writing reconstructions to recons.
requirements: If n > 0, x must point to at least n query vectors.
distances and labels must have capacity for n * k results.
recons must have capacity for n * k reconstructed vectors in the original input dimensionality.
k must be >= 1.
params, if provided, must be compatible; SearchParametersPreTransform can be used to forward sub-index parameters.
Reconstruction may be approximate or unsupported depending on transforms; caller should handle such cases.

functions.name: faiss::IndexPreTransform::apply_chain
functions.signature: const float* faiss::IndexPreTransform::apply_chain(faiss::idx_t n, const float* x) const
functions.description: Applies the configured transform chain to n input vectors x and returns a pointer to the transformed data. The returned pointer may alias x; otherwise, the returned buffer is newly allocated and should be deallocated by the caller.
requirements: If n > 0, x must point to at least n input vectors with the expected dimensionality.

Caller must determine whether the returned pointer equals x; if different, the caller is responsible for deallocating the returned buffer. The deallocation mechanism is not specified here and follows library conventions.
Transforms in the chain must be properly initialized/trained as required.

functions.name: faiss::IndexPreTransform::reverse_chain
functions.signature: void faiss::IndexPreTransform::reverse_chain(faiss::idx_t n, const float* xt, float* x) const
functions.description: Attempts to reverse the transform chain on n transformed vectors xt, writing the approximated or exact original-space vectors into x. Not all transforms may support inversion and results may be approximate.
requirements: If n > 0, xt must point to at least n vectors in the transformed space that matches the chain’s output dimensionality, and x must point to a buffer for at least n vectors in the original input dimensionality.
Behavior is undefined for transforms that do not support reversal; caller should not assume exact inversion.

functions.name: faiss::IndexPreTransform::get_distance_computer
functions.signature: faiss::DistanceComputer* faiss::IndexPreTransform::get_distance_computer() const
functions.description: Returns a DistanceComputer configured for this index that computes distances in the transformed/index space. Useful for low-level distance computations consistent with the index configuration.
requirements: Returned pointer validity and ownership/lifetime are not specified here; caller must consult the implementation to determine whether it must be deleted.
May return nullptr if not supported by the sub-index.

functions.name: faiss::IndexPreTransform::sa_code_size
functions.signature: size_t faiss::IndexPreTransform::sa_code_size() const
functions.description: Returns the number of bytes required to encode a single vector with the standalone codec interface of this index.
requirements: The value is determined by the configured transforms and sub-index; callers should use n * sa_code_size() when allocating buffers for encoding n vectors.

functions.name: faiss::IndexPreTransform::sa_encode
functions.signature: void faiss::IndexPreTransform::sa_encode(faiss::idx_t n, const float* x, uint8_t* bytes) const
functions.description: Encodes n input vectors x into the standalone byte representation produced by this index, writing n * sa_code_size() bytes into bytes.
requirements: If n > 0, x must point to at least n input vectors; bytes must point to a buffer of at least n * sa_code_size() bytes.
Transforms and sub-index components involved in encoding must be initialized/trained as required.

functions.name: faiss::IndexPreTransform::sa_decode
functions.signature: void faiss::IndexPreTransform::sa_decode(faiss::idx_t n, const uint8_t* bytes, float* x) const
functions.description: Decodes n vectors from the standalone byte representation into floating-point vectors in the appropriate space, writing to x.
requirements: If n > 0, bytes must point to at least n * sa_code_size() bytes; x must point to a buffer for at least n vectors with the appropriate dimensionality.
Decoding support depends on the configured transforms/index.

functions.name: faiss::IndexPreTransform::merge_from
functions.signature: void faiss::IndexPreTransform::merge_from(faiss::Index& otherIndex, faiss::idx_t add_id = 0)
functions.description: Merges the contents of otherIndex into this index, optionally offsetting ids by add_id. Typically requires both indexes to be compatible in configuration and dimensionality.
requirements: otherIndex must be compatible for merge; use check_compatible_for_merge to verify prior to calling.
add_id is an id offset applied to imported vectors' ids; must be chosen to avoid id collisions in the target index.
During merge, both indexes must remain valid; behavior on failure depends on implementations.

functions.name: faiss::IndexPreTransform::check_compatible_for_merge
functions.signature: void faiss::IndexPreTransform::check_compatible_for_merge(const faiss::Index& otherIndex) const
functions.description: Checks whether otherIndex is compatible with this index for merging. Typically validates dimensionality, metric type, and transform chain compatibility.
requirements: otherIndex must be a valid faiss::Index reference.
If incompatible, this function is expected to signal an error (e.g., via exception) per implementation; callers should handle errors before calling merge_from.

functions.name: faiss::IndexPreTransform::~IndexPreTransform
functions.signature: faiss::IndexPreTransform::~IndexPreTransform()
functions.description: Destructor for IndexPreTransform. If own_fields is true, it deletes owned pointers (transforms and/or sub-index). Otherwise, it does not delete external resources.
requirements: All ownership semantics depend on own_fields; callers must ensure no double-deletion or leaks by configuring ownership appropriately.
Do not use the object after destruction.

functions.name: faiss::VectorTransform::train
functions.signature: virtual void faiss::VectorTransform::train(faiss::idx_t n, const float* x)
functions.description: Trains the vector transform on a representative set of n input vectors. Default implementation does nothing (transform is considered already trained or training not required). Use in subclasses that need statistics learned from data.
requirements: x must point to at least n * d_in floats
n may be 0 if the transform does not require training
Call this before apply/apply_noalloc if the specific transform requires training (see is_trained)

functions.name: faiss::VectorTransform::apply
functions.signature: float* faiss::VectorTransform::apply(faiss::idx_t n, const float* x) const
functions.description: Applies the transformation to n input vectors and returns a newly allocated array of transformed vectors of size n * d_out. Convenience wrapper that allocates the output and calls apply_noalloc.
requirements: x must point to at least n * d_in floats
The transform should be trained if training is required (is_trained == true)
Caller is responsible for freeing the returned array (allocated to hold n * d_out floats)

functions.name: faiss::VectorTransform::apply_noalloc
functions.signature: virtual void faiss::VectorTransform::apply_noalloc(faiss::idx_t n, const float* x, float* xt) const = 0
functions.description: Applies the transformation to n input vectors, writing results into the provided buffer xt. Implemented by subclasses.
requirements: x must point to at least n * d_in floats
xt must point to a writable buffer of at least n * d_out floats
The transform should be trained if training is required (is_trained == true)

functions.name: faiss::VectorTransform::reverse_transform
functions.signature: virtual void faiss::VectorTransform::reverse_transform(faiss::idx_t n, const float* xt, float* x) const
functions.description: Attempts to reverse the transformation on n transformed vectors xt into x. Not all transforms implement an exact inverse; the result may be approximate or unimplemented in subclasses.
requirements: xt must point to at least n * d_out floats
x must point to a writable buffer of at least n * d_in floats
May be a no-op or approximate depending on the subclass; callers should not assume perfect reconstruction unless documented by the subclass

functions.name: faiss::VectorTransform::check_identical
functions.signature: virtual void faiss::VectorTransform::check_identical(const faiss::VectorTransform& other) const = 0
functions.description: Checks that two transforms are identical, typically for merging indexes. Implemented by subclasses to compare configuration and learned parameters.
requirements: other must be the same concrete transform type and have identical parameters/state as required by the subclass
May signal non-identity via exception/assertion depending on implementation

functions.name: faiss::LinearTransform::LinearTransform
functions.signature: explicit faiss::LinearTransform::LinearTransform(int d_in = 0, int d_out = 0, bool have_bias = false)
functions.description: Constructs a linear transform y = A * x + b with specified input/output dimensions and optional bias. A and b are initially empty; training or manual setup is expected before use.
requirements: d_in and d_out define the expected input/output dimensions for subsequent calls
If have_bias is true, b must be sized to d_out before applying the transform (via training or preparation)

functions.name: faiss::LinearTransform::apply_noalloc
functions.signature: void faiss::LinearTransform::apply_noalloc(faiss::idx_t n, const float* x, float* xt) const
functions.description: Applies the linear transform y = A * x + b to n vectors, writing results into xt. Supports both dimensionality reduction and expansion.
requirements: x must point to at least n * d_in floats
xt must point to a writable buffer of at least n * d_out floats
A must be sized to d_out * d_in; if have_bias == true, b must be sized to d_out
The transform should be trained/prepared so that A (and b if used) are set

functions.name: faiss::LinearTransform::transform_transpose
functions.signature: void faiss::LinearTransform::transform_transpose(faiss::idx_t n, const float* y, float* x) const
functions.description: Computes x = A^T * (y - b) for n vectors, i.e., applies the transpose of the linear map after removing bias. This equals the reverse transform when A has orthonormal rows.
requirements: y must point to at least n * d_out floats
x must point to a writable buffer of at least n * d_in floats
A must be sized to d_out * d_in; if have_bias == true, b must be sized to d_out

functions.name: faiss::LinearTransform::reverse_transform
functions.signature: void faiss::LinearTransform::reverse_transform(faiss::idx_t n, const float* xt, float* x) const
functions.description: Reconstructs x from xt using the inverse mapping when possible. For LinearTransform, this works only if the matrix A has orthonormal rows (is_orthonormal).
requirements: xt must point to at least n * d_out floats
x must point to a writable buffer of at least n * d_in floats
Only reliable if is_orthonormal is true; otherwise the result may be invalid

functions.name: faiss::LinearTransform::set_is_orthonormal
functions.signature: void faiss::LinearTransform::set_is_orthonormal()
functions.description: Computes A^T * A to determine whether A has orthonormal rows and sets the is_orthonormal flag accordingly. Enables accurate reverse_transform when true.
requirements: A must be initialized and sized to d_out * d_in before calling

functions.name: faiss::LinearTransform::print_if_verbose
functions.signature: void faiss::LinearTransform::print_if_verbose(const char* name, const std::vector<double>& mat, int n, int d) const
functions.description: If verbose is enabled, prints a matrix (mat) with given dimensions and label name for debugging/inspection purposes. No effect when verbose is false.

name should be a valid null-terminated string pointer if printing occurs

functions.name: faiss::LinearTransform::check_identical
functions.signature: void faiss::LinearTransform::check_identical(const faiss::VectorTransform& other) const
functions.description: Checks that another transform is an identical LinearTransform (same A, b, dimensions, and flags). Used for merging indexes safely.

functions.name: faiss::RandomRotationMatrix::RandomRotationMatrix
functions.signature: faiss::RandomRotationMatrix::RandomRotationMatrix(int d_in, int d_out)
functions.description: Constructs a random rotation linear transform (no bias) supporting dimensionality change. A must be initialized via init or train before applying.
requirements: d_in and d_out define the dimensions of A
Must call init(seed) or train(...) before first apply/apply_noalloc to initialize A

functions.name: faiss::RandomRotationMatrix::init
functions.signature: void faiss::RandomRotationMatrix::init(int seed)
functions.description: Initializes the random rotation matrix with a deterministic seed. Must be called before use (unless train is used to initialize).
requirements: Call before applying the transform if train(...) was not called
seed selects the random generator state; any integer is allowed

functions.name: faiss::RandomRotationMatrix::train
functions.signature: void faiss::RandomRotationMatrix::train(faiss::idx_t n, const float* x)
functions.description: Initializes the random rotation using an arbitrary seed. Training data are not used to fit parameters (only to satisfy the training interface).
requirements: May be called with any n; x is unused but should be a valid pointer if n > 0
After calling, the transform is initialized and can be applied

functions.name: faiss::PCAMatrix::PCAMatrix
functions.signature: explicit faiss::PCAMatrix::PCAMatrix(int d_in = 0, int d_out = 0, float eigen_power = 0, bool random_rotation = false)
functions.description: Constructs a PCA-based linear transform with optional whitening (via eigen_power) and optional random rotation. The final A and b are computed during training and preparation.
requirements: d_in and d_out set the PCA input and output dimensions
eigen_power controls scaling of components; epsilon is used internally to avoid division by zero when whitening
random_rotation indicates whether to apply a random rotation after PCA; requires training to materialize

functions.name: faiss::PCAMatrix::train
functions.signature: void faiss::PCAMatrix::train(faiss::idx_t n, const float* x)
functions.description: Trains PCA on n input vectors. If n < d_in, the eigenvector matrix is completed with zeros. Computes mean, eigenvalues, and PCAMat; may optionally perform whitening/rotation later.
requirements: x must point to at least n * d_in floats
n can be less than d_in; output eigenvectors will be zero-padded in that case
Call prepare_Ab() (internally or afterwards) before applying if required to finalize A and b

functions.name: faiss::PCAMatrix::copy_from
functions.signature: void faiss::PCAMatrix::copy_from(const faiss::PCAMatrix& other)
functions.description: Copies pre-trained PCA parameters (mean, eigenvalues, PCAMat, and derived matrices) from another PCAMatrix.
requirements: other must be a compatible PCAMatrix (same d_in/d_out) for copied parameters to be meaningful

functions.name: faiss::PCAMatrix::prepare_Ab
functions.signature: void faiss::PCAMatrix::prepare_Ab()
functions.description: Finalizes the linear transform matrices after mean, PCAMat, and eigenvalues are computed, applying whitening (eigen_power/epsilon) and optional random rotation to produce A and b.
requirements: mean, PCAMat, and eigenvalues must be computed/initialized before calling

functions.name: faiss::ITQMatrix::ITQMatrix
functions.signature: explicit faiss::ITQMatrix::ITQMatrix(int d = 0)
functions.description: Constructs the ITQ rotation matrix optimizer for binary coding in d dimensions. Parameters (e.g., max_iter, seed) can be configured before training.
requirements: d sets the working dimensionality; A will be learned during training

functions.name: faiss::ITQMatrix::train
functions.signature: void faiss::ITQMatrix::train(faiss::idx_t n, const float* x)
functions.description: Trains the ITQ rotation by alternating optimization to minimize quantization error for n input vectors. Produces a rotation matrix in A (and no bias).
requirements: x must point to at least n * d_in floats (d_in is the current transform input dimension)
Configure max_iter/seed as desired before training

functions.name: faiss::ITQTransform::ITQTransform
functions.signature: explicit faiss::ITQTransform::ITQTransform(int d_in = 0, int d_out = 0, bool do_pca = false)
functions.description: Constructs the full ITQ transform, optionally including PCA before ITQ. Produces binary-friendly projections by concatenating PCA and ITQ into a single LinearTransform.
requirements: d_in and d_out define input/output dimensionalities for the combined transform
If do_pca is true, PCA training will precede ITQ during train(...)

functions.name: faiss::ITQTransform::train
functions.signature: void faiss::ITQTransform::train(faiss::idx_t n, const float* x)
functions.description: Trains the ITQ transform: optionally centers/PCA-reduces data, then trains ITQMatrix and builds the concatenated LinearTransform pca_then_itq.
requirements: x must point to at least n * d_in floats
max_train_per_dim may limit the number of training points used internally

functions.name: faiss::ITQTransform::apply_noalloc
functions.signature: void faiss::ITQTransform::apply_noalloc(faiss::idx_t n, const float* x, float* xt) const
functions.description: Applies the trained ITQ (and optional PCA) transform to n input vectors into xt via the internal concatenated linear transform.
requirements: x must point to at least n * d_in floats
xt must point to a writable buffer of at least n * d_out floats
The transform must be trained so that pca_then_itq is prepared

functions.name: faiss::ITQTransform::check_identical
functions.signature: void faiss::ITQTransform::check_identical(const faiss::VectorTransform& other) const
functions.description: Checks deep equality with another transform, including mean, PCA configuration, ITQ rotation, and dimensions, to ensure merges are safe.
requirements: other must be an ITQTransform with identical parameters and learned state; otherwise the check fails (likely via exception/assert)

functions.name: faiss::OPQMatrix::OPQMatrix
functions.signature: explicit faiss::OPQMatrix::OPQMatrix(int d = 0, int M = 1, int d2 = -1)
functions.description: Constructs an OPQ rotation (block-wise) for M subquantizers over d dimensions, optionally producing d2-dimensional outputs. Used to minimize PQ reconstruction error.
requirements: d sets the input dimensionality; M must be the intended number of subquantizers
If d2 != -1, the output dimension is d2; otherwise it defaults to d

functions.name: faiss::OPQMatrix::train
functions.signature: void faiss::OPQMatrix::train(faiss::idx_t n, const float* x)
functions.description: Trains the OPQ rotation using alternating optimization with an internal or provided ProductQuantizer to minimize reconstruction error.
requirements: x must point to at least n * d_in floats
If pq is non-null, it should be constructed for (d_out, M, _ ) as documented
Large n may be sub-sampled internally to max_train_points

functions.name: faiss::RemapDimensionsTransform::RemapDimensionsTransform
functions.signature: faiss::RemapDimensionsTransform::RemapDimensionsTransform(int d_in, int d_out, const int* map)
functions.description: Constructs a dimension remapping transform from input to output dimensions using an explicit map array of length d_out; -1 entries output zeros.
requirements: map must point to at least d_out integers

functions.name: faiss::RemapDimensionsTransform::apply_noalloc
functions.signature: void faiss::RemapDimensionsTransform::apply_noalloc(faiss::idx_t n, const float* x, float* xt) const
functions.description: Applies the dimension remapping to n vectors, copying/zero-filling as dictated by map or the uniform rule.
requirements: x must point to at least n * d_in floats
xt must point to a writable buffer of at least n * d_out floats

functions.name: faiss::RemapDimensionsTransform::reverse_transform
functions.signature: void faiss::RemapDimensionsTransform::reverse_transform(faiss::idx_t n, const float* xt, float* x) const
functions.description: Attempts to invert the remapping for n vectors. Exact only when the mapping is a permutation; otherwise information loss prevents perfect inversion.
requirements: xt must point to at least n * d_out floats
x must point to a writable buffer of at least n * d_in floats
Only correct when the mapping is a permutation; otherwise treated as approximate

functions.name: faiss::RemapDimensionsTransform::check_identical
functions.signature: void faiss::RemapDimensionsTransform::check_identical(const faiss::VectorTransform& other) const
functions.description: Checks that another transform has the same remapping (same map/dimensions).
requirements: other must be a RemapDimensionsTransform with identical map and dimensions; otherwise the check fails (likely via exception/assert)

functions.name: faiss::NormalizationTransform::NormalizationTransform
functions.signature: explicit faiss::NormalizationTransform::NormalizationTransform(int d, float norm = 2.0f)
functions.description: Constructs a per-vector normalization transform of dimension d, using the specified norm (e.g., L2 when norm=2).
requirements: d sets both input and output dimensions
norm specifies the normalization order; exact behavior outside standard values depends on implementation

functions.name: faiss::NormalizationTransform::apply_noalloc
functions.signature: void faiss::NormalizationTransform::apply_noalloc(faiss::idx_t n, const float* x, float* xt) const
functions.description: Normalizes each input vector to the specified norm independently and writes the result to xt.

xt must point to a writable buffer of at least n * d_out floats

functions.name: faiss::NormalizationTransform::reverse_transform
functions.signature: void faiss::NormalizationTransform::reverse_transform(faiss::idx_t n, const float* xt, float* x) const
