requirements: xt must point to at least n * d_out floats
x must point to a writable buffer of at least n * d_in floats

functions.name: faiss::NormalizationTransform::check_identical
functions.signature: void faiss::NormalizationTransform::check_identical(const faiss::VectorTransform& other) const
functions.description: Checks that another transform has identical normalization parameters and dimensions.
requirements: other must be a NormalizationTransform with identical settings; otherwise the check fails (likely via exception/assert)

functions.name: faiss::CenteringTransform::CenteringTransform
functions.signature: explicit faiss::CenteringTransform::CenteringTransform(int d = 0)
functions.description: Constructs a centering transform of dimension d that subtracts (and can later add back) the per-dimension mean.
requirements: d sets both input and output dimensions

functions.name: faiss::CenteringTransform::train
functions.signature: void faiss::CenteringTransform::train(faiss::idx_t n, const float* x)
functions.description: Computes the per-dimension mean from n training vectors to be subtracted during application.
requirements: x must point to at least n * d_in floats
Call before applying so that mean is set

functions.name: faiss::CenteringTransform::apply_noalloc
functions.signature: void faiss::CenteringTransform::apply_noalloc(faiss::idx_t n, const float* x, float* xt) const
functions.description: Subtracts the learned mean from each of the n input vectors and writes the centered vectors to xt.
requirements: x must point to at least n * d_in floats
xt must point to a writable buffer of at least n * d_out floats
Requires that mean has been trained or otherwise initialized

functions.name: faiss::CenteringTransform::reverse_transform
functions.signature: void faiss::CenteringTransform::reverse_transform(faiss::idx_t n, const float* xt, float* x) const
functions.description: Adds the learned mean back to the centered vectors to reconstruct the original scale.
requirements: xt must point to at least n * d_out floats
x must point to a writable buffer of at least n * d_in floats
Requires that mean has been trained or otherwise initialized

functions.name: faiss::CenteringTransform::check_identical
functions.signature: void faiss::CenteringTransform::check_identical(const faiss::VectorTransform& other) const
functions.description: Checks that another transform has the same centering parameters (mean and dimensions).
requirements: other must be a CenteringTransform with identical mean and dimensions; otherwise the check fails (likely via exception/assert)

functions.name: faiss::AutoTuneCriterion::AutoTuneCriterion
functions.signature: faiss::AutoTuneCriterion::AutoTuneCriterion(idx_t nq, idx_t nnn)
functions.description: Constructs an evaluation criterion with the number of queries (nq) and number of nearest neighbors to request per query (nnn). Intended to be used to evaluate search results against ground truth after setting ground truth.
requirements: nq must be the number of queries that will be evaluated.
nnn must be the number of nearest neighbors that will be requested/provided to evaluate().

functions.name: faiss::AutoTuneCriterion::set_groundtruth
functions.signature: void faiss::AutoTuneCriterion::set_groundtruth(int gt_nnn, const float* gt_D_in, const idx_t* gt_I_in)
functions.description: Initializes the ground-truth distances and indices used by the evaluation criterion. Must be called before evaluate().
requirements: gt_nnn must be the number of ground-truth neighbors per query.
gt_D_in must point to an array of size nq * gt_nnn containing ground-truth distances.
gt_I_in must point to an array of size nq * gt_nnn containing ground-truth indices.
gt_D_in and gt_I_in must remain valid for the lifetime of the evaluation or until the data is internally copied (implementation-defined).
Must be called before any call to evaluate().

functions.name: faiss::AutoTuneCriterion::evaluate
functions.signature: virtual double faiss::AutoTuneCriterion::evaluate(const float* D, const idx_t* I) const
functions.description: Evaluates the configured criterion on the provided result distances and indices, returning a performance measure in [0, 1] where higher is better.
requirements: set_groundtruth() must have been called beforehand to initialize ground truth.
D must point to an array of size nq * nnn containing result distances.
I must point to an array of size nq * nnn containing result indices.
D and I must correspond to the same nq queries and nnn results as configured in the criterion.

functions.name: faiss::AutoTuneCriterion::~AutoTuneCriterion
functions.signature: virtual faiss::AutoTuneCriterion::~AutoTuneCriterion()
functions.description: Virtual destructor for AutoTuneCriterion, enabling safe deletion via base pointers.

functions.name: faiss::OneRecallAtRCriterion::OneRecallAtRCriterion
functions.signature: faiss::OneRecallAtRCriterion::OneRecallAtRCriterion(idx_t nq, idx_t R)
functions.description: Constructs a criterion that measures 1-recall at R (whether at least one true neighbor is found among the top-R retrieved) over nq queries.
requirements: nq must be the number of queries that will be evaluated.
R must be the cutoff for recall measurement per query.

functions.name: faiss::OneRecallAtRCriterion::evaluate
functions.signature: double faiss::OneRecallAtRCriterion::evaluate(const float* D, const idx_t* I) const
functions.description: Computes the 1-recall@R over the provided result sets, returning a value in [0, 1]. Uses the previously set ground truth to check if any of the top-R results per query matches.
requirements: AutoTuneCriterion::set_groundtruth() must have been called with appropriate ground-truth arrays.
I must point to an array of size nq * nnn containing retrieved indices; only the top-R per query are used for recall@R.
D must point to an array of size nq * nnn; distances may be unused for this criterion but must be valid pointers as per interface.
R must be less than or equal to nnn (the number of results provided per query).

functions.name: faiss::OneRecallAtRCriterion::~OneRecallAtRCriterion
functions.signature: faiss::OneRecallAtRCriterion::~OneRecallAtRCriterion()
functions.description: Destructor for OneRecallAtRCriterion.

functions.name: faiss::IntersectionCriterion::IntersectionCriterion
functions.signature: faiss::IntersectionCriterion::IntersectionCriterion(idx_t nq, idx_t R)
functions.description: Constructs a criterion that measures an intersection-based metric at cutoff R over nq queries. Exact definition is not documented here; inferred from name to compare overlap between result and ground-truth sets.
requirements: nq must be the number of queries that will be evaluated.
R must be the cutoff determining how many results per query are considered in the intersection metric.

functions.name: faiss::IntersectionCriterion::evaluate
functions.signature: double faiss::IntersectionCriterion::evaluate(const float* D, const idx_t* I) const
functions.description: Evaluates the intersection-based criterion at cutoff R on the provided result sets, returning a value in [0, 1]. Specific formula is not documented here; inferred as the fraction of overlap between retrieved top-R and ground-truth.
requirements: AutoTuneCriterion::set_groundtruth() must have been called with appropriate ground-truth arrays.
I must point to an array of size nq * nnn containing retrieved indices; at least the top-R per query are considered.
D must point to an array of size nq * nnn; distances may be unused for this criterion but must be valid pointers as per interface.
R must be less than or equal to nnn (the number of results provided per query).

functions.name: faiss::IntersectionCriterion::~IntersectionCriterion
functions.signature: faiss::IntersectionCriterion::~IntersectionCriterion()
functions.description: Destructor for IntersectionCriterion.

functions.name: faiss::Clustering::Clustering
functions.signature: faiss::Clustering::Clustering(int d, int k)
functions.description: Constructor for a k-means Clustering object with given vector dimension and number of centroids. Use when default ClusteringParameters are acceptable.
requirements: d must match the dimensionality of any training vectors subsequently provided (size n*d).
k is the number of centroids to learn; must be >= 1 for a meaningful clustering.
If centroids are pre-filled in the centroids vector before training, they will be used for initialization.

functions.name: faiss::Clustering::Clustering
functions.signature: faiss::Clustering::Clustering(int d, int k, const faiss::ClusteringParameters& cp)
functions.description: Constructor for a k-means Clustering object with explicit clustering parameters controlling iterations, initialization, normalization, etc.
requirements: d must match the dimensionality of any training vectors subsequently provided (size n*d).
k is the number of centroids to learn; must be >= 1 for a meaningful clustering.
cp fields govern behavior (e.g., niter, nredo, spherical, int_centroids, seed, init_method, etc.).
If centroids are pre-filled in the centroids vector before training, they will be used for initialization.

functions.name: faiss::Clustering::train
functions.signature: virtual void faiss::Clustering::train(faiss::idx_t n, const float* x, faiss::Index& index, const float* x_weights = nullptr)
functions.description: Run k-means training using a faiss::Index for point-to-centroid assignment. Centroids are added to the index at each iteration; on output, centroids holds the final centroids and they remain added to the index. If centroids is non-empty on input, it is used for initialization.
requirements: x points to n*d floats, where d equals the Clustering::d provided at construction.
n can be 0 or more; practical clustering requires n >= k and n > 0.
index must accept adding d-dimensional centroids and support assignment (search) used internally by clustering.
x_weights is either nullptr or points to n floats (weights per vector).
If ClusteringParameters::spherical is true, centroids will be L2-normalized after each update; if int_centroids is true, centroids are rounded to nearest integers.
If ClusteringParameters::frozen_centroids is true and centroids are provided on input, they will be used and not updated during iterations.
If ClusteringParameters::check_input_data_for_NaNs is true, NaN inputs may be rejected.
Training set may be subsampled based on max_points_per_centroid and related parameters; fewer than 1 point per centroid raises an exception (per comments).

functions.name: faiss::Clustering::train_encoded
functions.signature: void faiss::Clustering::train_encoded(faiss::idx_t nx, const uint8_t* x_in, const faiss::Index* codec, faiss::Index& index, const float* weights = nullptr)
functions.description: Run k-means training with encoded input vectors. Uses a codec (Index) to decode batches of the input before assignment via the provided index. If codec is nullptr, inputs are treated as raw floats rather than encoded.
requirements: nx is the number of training vectors; practical clustering requires nx >= k and nx > 0.
If codec is not nullptr, x_in points to the encoded representation expected by codec; decoding may occur in blocks of size decode_block_size.
If codec is nullptr, x_in must actually point to float data laid out as nx*d floats (despite the uint8_t* type), and will be treated as raw floats (per comment).
index must accept adding d-dimensional centroids and support assignment (search) used internally by clustering.
weights is either nullptr or points to nx floats (weights per vector).
ClusteringParameters::decode_block_size controls batch decoding size when codec is used.
Other behavior (spherical, int_centroids, frozen_centroids, etc.) follows Clustering::train semantics.

functions.name: faiss::index_factory
functions.signature: faiss::Index* faiss::index_factory(int d, const char* description, faiss::MetricType metric = faiss::METRIC_L2, bool own_invlists = true);
functions.description: Constructs and returns a float/vector Index according to a textual factory description. The description encodes a sequence of processing/indexing steps (e.g., IVF, PQ, HNSW). Use this to quickly create composite FAISS indexes without manual wiring. The metric selects the distance/similarity used by the resulting index (e.g., L2, inner product). If the created index is IVF-based, own_invlists controls whether the index owns its inverted lists. On invalid or unsupported descriptions/configurations, the function is expected to fail (typically via exception in FAISS builds).
requirements: d must be a positive integer (> 0) and must match the dimensionality of all vectors subsequently added to the index.
description must be a valid, null-terminated C string using FAISS factory syntax describing the index pipeline; invalid or unsupported tokens/combinations are not allowed.
metric must be a valid faiss::MetricType supported by the constructed index (e.g., some index types only support specific metrics).

If the resulting index is IVF-based and own_invlists is false, the index will not own its inverted lists; callers must ensure compatible external inverted lists management and lifetime before using the index.
The returned pointer is heap-allocated; the caller is responsible for destroying the index to avoid memory leaks (e.g., delete or appropriate FAISS destruction mechanism).
Thread-safety of construction is not guaranteed by this API; callers should avoid concurrent calls using shared mutable state.

functions.description: Constructs and returns a binary IndexBinary according to a textual factory description for binary indexing. Intended for Hamming-like binary vector search, it builds the requested binary index pipeline from the description string. If the created index is IVF-based, own_invlists controls whether the index owns its inverted lists. On invalid or unsupported descriptions/configurations, the function is expected to fail (typically via exception in FAISS builds).
requirements: d must be a positive integer (> 0) and must match the bit-length dimensionality of all binary vectors subsequently added to the index.
description must be a valid, null-terminated C string using FAISS binary factory syntax describing the index; invalid or unsupported tokens/combinations are not allowed.

If the resulting index is IVF-based and own_invlists is false, the index will not own its inverted lists; callers must ensure compatible external inverted lists management and lifetime before using the index.
The returned pointer is heap-allocated; the caller is responsible for destroying the index to avoid memory leaks (e.g., delete or appropriate FAISS destruction mechanism).
Thread-safety of construction is not guaranteed by this API; callers should avoid concurrent calls using shared mutable state.

functions.name: faiss::read_index
functions.signature: Index* faiss::read_index(const char* fname, int io_flags = 0)
functions.description: Deserialize a Faiss Index from a file path. Returns a newly allocated Index that the caller must delete. Optional I/O flags influence how data is loaded (e.g., read-only, mmap, skip IVF data).
requirements: fname must be a valid, readable filesystem path
io_flags is a bitwise OR of IO_FLAG_* constants; some flags are implemented only for a subset of index types
If IO_FLAG_READ_ONLY is set, returned index may operate in read-only mode (implementation dependent)
If IO_FLAG_ONDISK_SAME_DIR is set, strip directory components from on-disk filenames and look relative to the index file directory
If IO_FLAG_SKIP_IVF_DATA is set, IVF data is not loaded to RAM (only list sizes)
If IO_FLAG_SKIP_PRECOMPUTE_TABLE is set, do not initialize precomputed tables after loading
If IO_FLAG_PQ_SKIP_SDC_TABLE is set, do not compute the SDC table for PQ-based indices (prevents certain distance computations and may prevent graph building)
If IO_FLAG_MMAP is set, try to memory-map data where supported
If IO_FLAG_MMAP_IFC is set, try to mmap codes for IndexFlatCodes-derived indices and HNSW (temporary/limited)
Returned pointer must be deleted by the caller using delete
All references within the returned object are owned by the object itself

Before adding/searching, the index should be appropriately trained (inferred from FAISS IndexIVF patterns)

functions.name: faiss::IndexLattice::IndexLattice
functions.signature: faiss::IndexLattice::IndexLattice(idx_t d, int nsq, int scale_nbit, int r2)
functions.description: Constructor for an IndexLattice, an IndexFlatCodes-based quantizer that encodes vectors with a series of Zn lattice quantizers. Initializes the index dimensionality (d), number of sub-vectors (nsq), the number of bits used to encode the per-subvector scale (scale_nbit), and a lattice/radius parameter (r2). Details of lattice_nbit and derived parameters are determined internally. Usage: construct the index with the target dimensionality and quantization parameters, then call train() before encoding/adding vectors. Notes: dsq (subvector dimension) is derived from d and nsq. Some constraints (e.g., d divisible by nsq) are typical for subquantizers and are inferred from member names; concrete validation behavior is not shown in this header.
requirements: d must be the full dimensionality of vectors provided to train/encode (inferred from Index API).
nsq is the number of sub-vectors; typically d should be divisible by nsq so that dsq = d / nsq (inferred from naming and common FAISS patterns).
scale_nbit must be non-negative; its effect is to control bits allocated to scale quantization (inferred; exact valid range unknown).
r2 configures the lattice quantizer (inferred from parameter name and Zn lattice context); acceptable range is unknown.
The constructed object should be trained via train() before encoding vectors with sa_encode (inferred from presence of trained stats).

functions.name: faiss::IndexLattice::train

functions.description: Trains the Zn lattice quantizer parameters of this IndexLattice on n training vectors x of dimensionality d. Establishes subquantizer norm ranges and any codec tables needed for subsequent encoding. Usage: call once (or as needed) before sa_encode/adding vectors, providing representative training data of size n × d.
requirements: If n > 0, x must point to an array of at least n * d floats laid out row-major (contiguous) where d is the index dimensionality (inferred from FAISS conventions).
x must not be null when n > 0 (inferred).
n must be >= 0 (inferred).
Input vectors should be finite numeric values; NaNs/Infs may lead to undefined training behavior (inferred).
Must be called before sa_encode to ensure the codec has valid trained parameters (inferred from presence of trained stats).

functions.name: faiss::IndexLattice::sa_code_size
functions.signature: size_t faiss::IndexLattice::sa_code_size() const
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of the standalone-encoded code for a single vector using this lattice codec configuration. Use this to size output buffers for sa_encode and input buffers for sa_decode.

functions.name: faiss::IndexLattice::sa_encode
functions.signature: void faiss::IndexLattice::sa_encode(idx_t n, const float* x, uint8_t* bytes) const
functions.description: Encodes n input vectors x (each of dimension d) into the standalone byte representation produced by the Zn lattice codec, writing n consecutive codes to bytes. The per-vector code size is given by sa_code_size(). Intended for batch encoding suitable for storage or use with IndexFlatCodes.
requirements: train() should be successfully run before encoding so that codec parameters are initialized (inferred from presence of trained stats).
If n > 0, x must point to at least n * d floats in row-major contiguous layout (inferred from FAISS conventions).
bytes must point to writable storage of at least n * sa_code_size() bytes (inferred).
x and bytes must not be null when n > 0 (inferred).
Input values should be finite; extreme values outside trained ranges may quantize poorly (inferred).

functions.name: faiss::IndexLattice::sa_decode
functions.signature: void faiss::IndexLattice::sa_decode(idx_t n, const uint8_t* bytes, float* x) const
functions.description: Decodes n standalone lattice codes from bytes back into reconstructed floating-point vectors, writing n × d floats to x. The input is expected to be produced by the same or a configuration-compatible IndexLattice (same nsq/bit configuration).
requirements: If n > 0, bytes must point to at least n * sa_code_size() bytes; codes should be produced by a compatible IndexLattice configuration (inferred).
If n > 0, x must point to writable storage for at least n * d floats (inferred).
bytes and x must not be null when n > 0 (inferred).
Decoding assumes the codec configuration matches the one used for encoding; mismatched parameters can produce incorrect output (inferred).

own_invlists determines ownership of inverted lists; when true the index manages their lifetime (inferred from FAISS patterns)

If own_fields is false (default) and you assign external objects, you must manage their lifetimes yourself unless you later set own_fields to true and transfer ownership in a manner consistent with the implementation.

x must be a valid, readable pointer; null is only allowed when n == 0.

functions.description: Constructs an IndexNeuralNetCodec, an IndexFlatCodes-based index that encodes vectors using a neural-network-driven codec into fixed-size codes. Use this to create an index with dimension d, with M code blocks and nbits per block, and a distance metric. Details of the codec behavior are defined by NeuralNetCodec and are not shown here.
requirements: d, M, and nbits should be non-negative integers; d typically should match the dimensionality of vectors that will be provided to train/encode/decode.
metric must be a valid faiss::MetricType value.
Object must be fully constructed before being used from multiple threads (standard C++ object construction requirement).

functions.name: faiss::IndexNeuralNetCodec::train
functions.signature: void faiss::IndexNeuralNetCodec::train(faiss::idx_t n, const float* x)
functions.description: Trains the neural network codec on n training vectors x (dimension d per vector). This prepares the codec parameters so subsequent encoding/decoding can produce meaningful codes. If the codec is already trained or training is unnecessary, this may be a no-op depending on the implementation of NeuralNetCodec (not shown here).
requirements: n must be >= 0.
x must point to at least n * d contiguous floats in row-major order, where d is the index dimensionality specified at construction.
The index dimensionality d used at construction must match the dimensionality of the input vectors x.
The instance must be in a valid state (constructed); training may need to be called before sa_encode if the codec requires training (inferred from FAISS patterns).
Thread-safety is not guaranteed; do not call train concurrently with other mutations on the same instance unless documented elsewhere.

functions.name: faiss::IndexNeuralNetCodec::sa_encode
functions.signature: void faiss::IndexNeuralNetCodec::sa_encode(faiss::idx_t n, const float* x, uint8_t* codes) const
functions.description: Batch-encodes n input vectors x into compact byte codes using the neural network codec. The output codes buffer receives one encoded code per input vector. Intended for stand-alone encoding routines in IndexFlatCodes-derived classes.
requirements: n must be >= 0.
x must point to at least n * d contiguous floats, where d is the index dimensionality specified at construction.
codes must point to enough writable bytes to hold n encoded vectors. Per-vector code size is implementation-defined; commonly it corresponds to M * nbits bits (rounded up to bytes).
If the codec requires training, train(...) should be successfully completed before calling sa_encode (inferred from FAISS patterns).
Input and output buffers must not overlap in undefined ways; codes must be writable; x must be readable.
Function is const; it does not modify the index state.

functions.name: faiss::IndexNeuralNetCodec::sa_decode
functions.signature: void faiss::IndexNeuralNetCodec::sa_decode(faiss::idx_t n, const uint8_t* codes, float* x) const
functions.description: Batch-decodes n codes back into reconstructed float vectors using the neural network codec. Produces one d-dimensional vector per input code. Intended for stand-alone decoding in IndexFlatCodes-derived classes.
requirements: n must be >= 0.

codes must point to at least the number of bytes required to represent n encoded vectors. Per-vector code size is implementation-defined; commonly it corresponds to M * nbits bits (rounded up to bytes).
x must point to enough writable memory for n * d floats, where d is the index dimensionality specified at construction.
If the codec requires training to define decoding parameters, train(...) should be completed before calling sa_decode (inferred).
Input and output buffers must not overlap in undefined ways; codes must be readable; x must be writable.
Function is const; it does not modify the index state.

functions.name: faiss::ivflib::search_centroid
functions.signature: void faiss::ivflib::search_centroid(faiss::Index* index, const float* x, int n, faiss::idx_t* centroid_ids)
functions.description: Computes, for each input vector, the id of the IVF coarse centroid (cluster) it belongs to. Intended for IVF indexes; for non-IVF indexes, meaningful clusters do not exist.

x must point to n vectors, each of dimension index->d (size n * d).

functions.name: faiss::ivflib::search_and_return_centroids
functions.signature: void faiss::ivflib::search_and_return_centroids(faiss::Index* index, size_t n, const float* xin, long k, float* distances, faiss::idx_t* labels, faiss::idx_t* query_centroid_ids, faiss::idx_t* result_centroid_ids)
functions.description: Performs a standard k-NN search on an IVF index and also returns the coarse centroid ids for each query and for each result. The other arguments are the same as the standard FAISS search.

xin must contain n query vectors of dimension index->d (size n * d).
k must be non-negative; if k > 0, distances and labels must have space for n * k entries.
distances must be a writable array of size n * k (or nullptr only if k == 0, per standard FAISS patterns).
labels must be a writable array of size n * k (or nullptr only if k == 0, per standard FAISS patterns).
query_centroid_ids must have space for n entries (one centroid id per query).
result_centroid_ids must have space for n * k entries (one centroid id per result).

functions.name: faiss::ivflib::SlidingIndexWindow::SlidingIndexWindow
functions.signature: faiss::ivflib::SlidingIndexWindow::SlidingIndexWindow(faiss::Index* index)

functions.name: faiss::ivflib::SlidingIndexWindow::step
functions.signature: void faiss::ivflib::SlidingIndexWindow::step(const faiss::Index* sub_index, bool remove_oldest)
functions.description: Adds one index slice to the window and (optionally) removes the oldest slice. Manages the FIFO sliding of concatenated IndexIVF slices.

functions.name: faiss::ivflib::set_invlist_range

functions.name: faiss::ivflib::search_with_parameters
functions.signature: void faiss::ivflib::search_with_parameters(const faiss::Index* index, faiss::idx_t n, const float* x, faiss::idx_t k, float* distances, faiss::idx_t* labels, const faiss::IVFSearchParameters* params, size_t* nb_dis = nullptr, double* ms_per_stage = nullptr)

functions.name: faiss::ivflib::range_search_with_parameters
functions.signature: void faiss::ivflib::range_search_with_parameters(const faiss::Index* index, faiss::idx_t n, const float* x, float radius, faiss::RangeSearchResult* result, const faiss::IVFSearchParameters* params, size_t* nb_dis = nullptr, double* ms_per_stage = nullptr)
functions.description: Performs a range search on an IVF index (possibly wrapped) using explicit IVF search parameters. Optionally returns statistics including the number of computed distances and per-stage timings.

functions.name: faiss::ivflib::ivf_residual_from_quantizer
functions.signature: faiss::ivflib::IndexIVFResidualQuantizer* faiss::ivflib::ivf_residual_from_quantizer(const faiss::ivflib::ResidualQuantizer& , int nlevel)
functions.description: Builds an IndexIVFResidualQuantizer from a ResidualQuantizer, using the first nlevel components as the coarse quantizer and the remaining components as codes stored in the inverted lists.

functions.name: faiss::ivflib::ivf_residual_add_from_flat_codes
functions.signature: void faiss::ivflib::ivf_residual_add_from_flat_codes(faiss::ivflib::IndexIVFResidualQuantizer* ivfrq, size_t ncode, const uint8_t* codes, int64_t code_size = -1)

functions.name: faiss::ivflib::DefaultShardingFunction::operator()
functions.signature: int64_t faiss::ivflib::DefaultShardingFunction::operator()(int64_t i, int64_t shard_count)
functions.description: Default sharding function used when sharding IVF centroids. By convention, it maps the ith vector to a shard, typically i mod shard_count.

functions.name: faiss::ivflib::shard_ivf_index_centroids
functions.signature: void faiss::ivflib::shard_ivf_index_centroids(faiss::IndexIVF* index, int64_t shard_count = 20, const std::string& filename_template = "shard.%d.index", faiss::ivflib::ShardingFunction* sharding_function = nullptr, bool generate_ids = false)

requirements: index must be a valid non-null faiss::IndexIVF pointer containing centroids already added to its quantizer.

If generate_ids is true, ids are generated using IndexIDMap2 to match the default ids of the unsharded index.

functions.name: faiss::ivflib::shard_binary_ivf_index_centroids

requirements: index must be a valid non-null faiss::IndexBinaryIVF pointer containing centroids already added to its quantizer.

filename_template should be a printf-style template accepting a shard id (e.g., "%d").

functions.name: faiss::IndexReplicasTemplate::IndexReplicasTemplate
functions.signature: explicit faiss::IndexReplicasTemplate<IndexT>::IndexReplicasTemplate(bool threaded = true)
functions.description: Constructs a replicated index wrapper that distributes calls to multiple sub-indices, optionally using one thread per sub-index. If threaded is true, each sub-index is managed by a separate CPU thread; otherwise, operations are performed sequentially.
requirements: No sub-index exists at construction; sub-indices are added later via add_replica().
If threaded is true, caller should expect concurrent execution across sub-indices; underlying sub-indices must be safe to call concurrently by this wrapper (as per faiss::ThreadedIndex semantics).
Behavior and performance depend on number of added sub-indices; initially there are none.

functions.name: faiss::IndexReplicasTemplate::IndexReplicasTemplate
functions.signature: explicit faiss::IndexReplicasTemplate<IndexT>::IndexReplicasTemplate(faiss::idx_t d, bool threaded = true)
functions.description: Constructs a replicated index wrapper with a fixed dimensionality d that all sub-indices must share, optionally using one thread per sub-index. Subsequent sub-index additions must match this dimension.
requirements: Parameter d sets the dimension that all sub-indices must share.
If threaded is true, the wrapper may run operations on sub-indices concurrently.
All sub-indices added via add_replica() must have dimension exactly d.

functions.name: faiss::IndexReplicasTemplate::IndexReplicasTemplate
functions.signature: explicit faiss::IndexReplicasTemplate<IndexT>::IndexReplicasTemplate(int d, bool threaded = true)
functions.description: Constructs a replicated index wrapper using an int-typed dimension value (to avoid implicit-conversion ambiguity with bool), with optional multi-threaded execution. Equivalent to the idx_t overload but with int-typed d.
requirements: Parameter d sets the dimension that all sub-indices must share; it must equal the sub-indices' dimensionality.
If threaded is true, the wrapper may run operations on sub-indices concurrently.

functions.name: faiss::IndexReplicasTemplate::add_replica
functions.signature: void faiss::IndexReplicasTemplate<IndexT>::add_replica(IndexT* index)
functions.description: Adds a sub-index (replica) to the wrapper. Alias for addIndex(); after addition, calls to train/add/search are dispatched across all replicas.
requirements: index must be a valid, non-null pointer to an IndexT instance.
The sub-index's dimensionality must match the wrapper's dimension. If no dimension has been set yet, the first added sub-index establishes it (per class comment).
Caller retains responsibility for ensuring the sub-index is in a valid state for subsequent operations (e.g., trained if required by its type).
Adding a sub-index enables its participation in later operations; order of addition may affect internal dimension initialization if not fixed at construction.

functions.name: faiss::IndexReplicasTemplate::remove_replica
functions.signature: void faiss::IndexReplicasTemplate<IndexT>::remove_replica(IndexT* index)
functions.description: Removes a previously added sub-index (replica) from the wrapper. Alias for removeIndex().
requirements: index must be a valid, non-null pointer and must refer to a sub-index previously added to this wrapper.
After removal, the sub-index no longer participates in train/add/search operations via this wrapper.

functions.name: faiss::IndexReplicasTemplate::train
functions.signature: void faiss::IndexReplicasTemplate<IndexT>::train(faiss::idx_t n, const component_t* x) override
functions.description: Trains all sub-indices using the same training data. The call is forwarded to each replica; if threaded mode is enabled, training may occur in parallel.
requirements: x must point to at least n * d contiguous components of type component_t, where d is the index dimensionality.
All currently added sub-indices receive the same call; behavior is that of each sub-index’s train() method.
n may be zero or greater as supported by the underlying sub-indices; minimum required n depends on sub-index type (unknown from this header).
x must remain valid for the duration of the call.

functions.name: faiss::IndexReplicasTemplate::add
functions.signature: void faiss::IndexReplicasTemplate<IndexT>::add(faiss::idx_t n, const component_t* x) override
functions.description: Adds n vectors to all sub-indices. The same data is forwarded to each replica; in threaded mode, addition may occur in parallel across replicas.
requirements: If the sub-index type requires prior training, the replicas must be trained before calling add() (requirement inferred from FAISS conventions; specific training prerequisites are not stated here).
x must point to at least n * d contiguous components of type component_t, where d is the index dimensionality.
x must remain valid for the duration of the call.
All currently added sub-indices receive the same call; failures or capacity constraints are governed by each sub-index’s add().

functions.name: faiss::IndexReplicasTemplate::search
functions.signature: void faiss::IndexReplicasTemplate<IndexT>::search(faiss::idx_t n, const component_t* x, faiss::idx_t k, distance_t* distances, faiss::idx_t* labels, const faiss::SearchParameters* params = nullptr) const override
functions.description: Searches all sub-indices by partitioning the n queries into approximately equal slices (ceil(n / number_of_indices)) and executing them across replicas (possibly in parallel). Results are joined into the output distances and labels arrays.
requirements: x must point to at least n * d contiguous components of type component_t.
k must be a positive integer (number of nearest neighbors to return).
distances must point to writable storage for at least n * k elements of type distance_t.
labels must point to writable storage for at least n * k elements of type idx_t.
params may be nullptr or must point to a SearchParameters instance acceptable to each sub-index.
Inputs must remain valid for the duration of the call.
Result semantics (e.g., metric, range handling) follow each sub-index’s search(); this wrapper partitions by queries and aggregates results.

functions.name: faiss::IndexReplicasTemplate::reconstruct
functions.signature: void faiss::IndexReplicasTemplate<IndexT>::reconstruct(faiss::idx_t, component_t* v) const override
functions.description: Reconstructs the vector corresponding to a given identifier by delegating to the first sub-index. This is useful for retrieving stored vector data.
requirements: The identifier (first argument) must be valid for the underlying first sub-index; behavior on invalid ids follows that sub-index’s reconstruct() (not specified here).
v must point to writable storage for at least d components of type component_t.
v must remain valid for the duration of the call.
At least one sub-index must be present; reconstruction uses the first sub-index.

functions.name: faiss::IndexReplicasTemplate::syncWithSubIndexes
functions.signature: void faiss::IndexReplicasTemplate<IndexT>::syncWithSubIndexes()
functions.description: Synchronizes the top-level replica index’s metadata/state with that of the sub-indices. Typical uses include updating properties such as total vector count or trained flags after sub-index changes.
requirements: Should be called after adding, removing, or mutating sub-indices to keep the wrapper’s state consistent.

functions.name: faiss::IndexShardsIVF::IndexShardsIVF
functions.signature: faiss::IndexShardsIVF::IndexShardsIVF(faiss::Index* quantizer, size_t nlist, bool threaded = false, bool successive_ids = true)
functions.description: Constructs an IndexShardsIVF that shards an IVF index across multiple sub-indexes while sharing a common coarse quantizer. Intended for distributed or sharded IVF setups where all shards use the same level-1 (coarse) quantizer and support precomputed coarse assignments. functions.name: faiss::IndexShardsIVF::addIndex
functions.signature: void faiss::IndexShardsIVF::addIndex(faiss::Index* index) override
functions.description: Adds a shard (sub-index) to the IndexShardsIVF. All added indexes must be IVF-like (implement IndexIVFInterface) so that search_precomputed can be used across shards and must be compatible with the shared coarse quantizer.

functions.signature: void faiss::IndexShardsIVF::add_with_ids(faiss::idx_t n, const faiss::component_t* x, const faiss::idx_t* xids) override

functions.name: faiss::IndexShardsIVF::train
functions.signature: void faiss::IndexShardsIVF::train(faiss::idx_t n, const faiss::component_t* x) override
functions.description: Trains the sharded IVF index (and/or its shared coarse quantizer) on n training vectors. Use prior to adding vectors if the index or its quantizer requires training.
requirements: If n > 0, x must be a valid pointer to at least n * d components, where d is the index dimensionality

functions.name: faiss::IndexShardsIVF::search
functions.signature: void faiss::IndexShardsIVF::search(faiss::idx_t n, const faiss::component_t* x, faiss::idx_t k, faiss::distance_t* distances, faiss::idx_t* labels, const faiss::SearchParameters* params = nullptr) const override

import os
import struct
import random
from typing import List

# We need to generate an initial buffer that FUZZ_PARAM_STR() will consume.
# The target stubs interpret FUZZ_PARAM_STR bytes as float32 matrices for
# training/add/search across many FAISS entry points. Provide a versatile,
# self-consistent payload containing:
# - A header with several small integers to drive choices (dimensions, sizes)
# - Multiple contiguous float32 matrices for different potential consumers
# - Fallback random bytes to cycle through if larger sizes are requested
#
# Constraints:
# - Return bytes (<= 4096 bytes)
# - Deterministic with seed, but varied
# - Values map well to float ranges used in stubs (avoid NaN/Inf)
#
# Layout (little-endian):
# [magic 4B] [params 16B = 4 uint32] then a sequence of float32 blocks.
# Blocks included:
#  - base vectors block A: nA * dA
#  - base vectors block B: nB * dB
#  - queries block Q: nQ * dQ
#  - generic buffer G: up to remaining capacity as float32s
# The dims (dA,dB,dQ) and counts are chosen small (<= 64) to match stubs.

MAGIC = 0xFA15FA15
MAX_BYTES = 4096


def _pack_u32(vals: List[int]) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('<' + 'I'*len(vals), *vals)


def _floats_to_bytes(floats: List[float]) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('<' + 'f'*len(floats), *floats)


def _gen_float32_values(rng: random.Random, count: int, mode: int) -> List[float]:
    vals: List[float] = []
    for i in range(count):
        # Mix several distributions to cover [-1,1], small Gaussians, and wider ranges
        sel = (mode + i) % 4
        if sel == 0:
            v = (rng.randint(0, 255) - 128) / 127.5  # ~[-1,1]
        elif sel == 1:
            v = rng.gauss(0.0, 0.5)  # small gaussian
        elif sel == 2:
            v = (rng.randint(0, 1000) - 500) / 250.0  # ~[-2,2]
        else:
            v = (rng.random() * 2.0) - 1.0  # uniform [-1,1]
        # Clamp to safe finite range for robustness
        if not (-1e6 < v < 1e6):
            v = 0.0
        vals.append(float(v))
    return vals


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose small dimensions and counts favored by stubs
    dA = rng.randint(4, 32)
    dB = rng.randint(1, 32)
    dQ = rng.randint(4, 32)
    nA = rng.randint(8, 64)
    nB = rng.randint(4, 48)
    nQ = rng.randint(1, 16)

    header = _pack_u32([MAGIC, dA, dB, dQ])

    # Build float blocks
    floatsA = _gen_float32_values(rng, nA * dA, mode=0)
    floatsB = _gen_float32_values(rng, nB * dB, mode=1)
    floatsQ = _gen_float32_values(rng, nQ * dQ, mode=2)

    body = b''.join([
        header,
        _floats_to_bytes(floatsA),
        _floats_to_bytes(floatsB),
        _floats_to_bytes(floatsQ),
    ])

    # Fill remaining space with additional float32s to act as a generic pool
    remaining = MAX_BYTES - len(body)
    if remaining < 0:
        # Trim if we somehow exceeded
        return body[:MAX_BYTES]

    # Reserve some space for a small trailing random byte pad (non-float consumers)
    pad_bytes = min(64, max(0, remaining // 8))
    remaining_floats_bytes = remaining - pad_bytes
    if remaining_floats_bytes > 0:
        extra_count = remaining_floats_bytes // 4
        extra_vals = _gen_float32_values(rng, extra_count, mode=3)
        body += _floats_to_bytes(extra_vals)
        remaining = MAX_BYTES - len(body)

    if remaining > 0:
        # Add a small random byte pad for code paths that read raw bytes
        pad = bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(remaining))
        body += pad

    # Ensure exact size limit
    if len(body) > MAX_BYTES:
        body = body[:MAX_BYTES]
    return body

import os
import random
from typing import List

# This generator targets FAISS binary-index fuzzers that consume arbitrary byte blobs
# via FUZZ_PARAM_STR. The stubs treat these strings as packed binary vectors
# (db and query) with sizes determined by d_bits/8. Therefore, validity hinges on:
# - Providing sufficiently long payloads so that requested buffers can be filled.
# - Including diversity to exercise different code paths (e.g., repeated patterns,
#   gradients, random noise) while remaining valid arbitrary bytes.
# We avoid malformed structures and focus on high-entropy but structured content.

MAX_OUTPUT = 4096

# Predefined interesting byte patterns to cover edge cases: all-zero, all-FF,
# alternating patterns, incrementing/decrementing, small cycles.
INTERESTING_PATTERNS: List[bytes] = [
    b"\x00" * 64,
    b"\xff" * 64,
    bytes([0x55]) * 64,  # 01010101
    bytes([0xAA]) * 64,  # 10101010
    bytes(range(64)),
    bytes(range(63, -1, -1)),
    (b"\x00\x01\x02\x03\x04\x05\x06\x07") * 8,
    (b"\xff\x00") * 32,
]


def rand_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))


def make_section(rng: random.Random, target_len: int) -> bytes:
    # Build a section by concatenating chunks chosen from patterns, random noise,
    # and short cycles. Keep it deterministic with the RNG.
    out = bytearray()
    while len(out) < target_len:
        choice = rng.randint(0, 5)
        remaining = target_len - len(out)
        # choose a chunk size biased to powers of two and small sizes
        base_sizes = [8, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 96, 128, 256]
        chunk = min(remaining, base_sizes[rng.randrange(len(base_sizes))])
        if choice == 0:
            # random noise
            out += rand_bytes(rng, chunk)
        elif choice == 1:
            # pick an interesting pattern and repeat/crop
            pat = INTERESTING_PATTERNS[rng.randrange(len(INTERESTING_PATTERNS))]
            reps = max(1, chunk // max(1, len(pat)))
            buf = (pat * reps)[:chunk]
            out += buf
        elif choice == 2:
            # small incrementing cycle from a random start
            start = rng.randrange(256)
            buf = bytes(((start + i) & 0xFF) for i in range(chunk))
            out += buf
        elif choice == 3:
            # small decrementing cycle
            start = rng.randrange(256)
            buf = bytes(((start - i) & 0xFF) for i in range(chunk))
            out += buf
        else:
            # two-byte alternating pattern derived from seed
            a = rng.randrange(256)
            b = rng.randrange(256)
            pair = bytes([a, b])
            reps = (chunk + 1) // 2
            buf = (pair * reps)[:chunk]
            out += buf
    return bytes(out[:target_len])


def assemble_payload(rng: random.Random, total_len: int) -> bytes:
    # To help multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls, provide multiple segments separated
    # by varied patterns, then shuffle a bit deterministically.
    segments = []
    # Split total into 3-6 sections
    n_sections = rng.randint(3, 6)
    remaining = total_len
    for i in range(n_sections):
        if i == n_sections - 1:
            seg_len = remaining
        else:
            # allocate a portion but leave room for remaining sections
            max_for_seg = max(1, remaining - (n_sections - i - 1))
            seg_len = rng.randint(1, max_for_seg)
        segments.append(make_section(rng, seg_len))
        remaining -= seg_len
    rng.shuffle(segments)
    payload = b"".join(segments)
    # Mix in a header/footer of structured bytes to seed early consumption
    header = INTERESTING_PATTERNS[rng.randrange(len(INTERESTING_PATTERNS))][:32]
    footer = INTERESTING_PATTERNS[rng.randrange(len(INTERESTING_PATTERNS))][:32]
    core = payload
    out = (header + core + footer)[:total_len]
    # Ensure non-empty and exact length
    if len(out) < total_len:
        out += rand_bytes(rng, total_len - len(out))
    return out[:total_len]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Choose total output size. The stubs cap consumption internally; provide a
    # robust buffer up to MAX_OUTPUT to satisfy multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls for
    # db and queries across varying d_bits.
    # Bias size towards mid-to-large to reduce early bailouts.
    sizes = [512, 768, 1024, 1536, 2048, 3072, 4096]
    total_len = sizes[rng.randrange(len(sizes))]
    total_len = min(total_len, MAX_OUTPUT)

    return assemble_payload(rng, total_len)

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Target data type: short alphanumeric/printable strings used as identifiers/names
# Fuzzer stubs also pull unsigned ints and floats from the same buffer source.
# We will craft a byte stream that interleaves:
# - Several compact printable strings (IDs/keys/parameter names), lengths <= 24
# - Unsigned ints in little-endian to provide bounded numeric values
# - Floats (IEEE-754) to exercise formatting paths
# The stream should be valid, reproducible with a seed, and under 4096 bytes.

def _rand_ascii(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    # Printable ASCII excluding control chars; include some punctuation and underscore
    alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_:.#@/"
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    s = ''.join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))
    return s.encode('ascii')

def _u32_le(x: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes((x & 0xFF, (x >> 8) & 0xFF, (x >> 16) & 0xFF, (x >> 24) & 0xFF))

def _f32_le(val: float) -> bytes:
    import struct
    return struct.pack('<f', val)

def _bounded_u32(rng: random.Random, max_inclusive: int) -> int:
    # produce a u32 that when modulo is applied, exercises edges near bounds
    choices = [0, 1, max_inclusive, max_inclusive - 1 if max_inclusive > 0 else 0]
    # mix in random
    choices.append(rng.randrange(0, 0xFFFFFFFF))
    return rng.choice(choices) & 0xFFFFFFFF

def _interesting_float(rng: random.Random) -> float:
    # Values that format nicely and cover edge cases
    specials = [0.0, -0.0, 1.0, -1.0, 1e-6, -1e-6, 1e6, -1e6, 3.1415926, -2.7182818]
    # also some random normal values
    specials.append(rng.uniform(-1000.0, 1000.0))
    return rng.choice(specials)

def _emit_string_block(rng: random.Random, out: List[bytes], label: str, min_len=1, max_len=24):
    # Prepend a small header for potential length; FUZZ_PARAM_STR typically ignores, but harmless
    s = _rand_ascii(rng, min_len, max_len)
    # Occasionally generate boundary lengths (empty or max)
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        s = b''
    elif rng.random() < 0.2:
        s = _rand_ascii(rng, max_len, max_len)
    # Header length then data, helping consumers that first read sizes
    out.append(_u32_le(len(s)))
    out.append(s)

def _emit_numbers_block(rng: random.Random, out: List[bytes]):
    # Unsigned ints used with various modulos (1000, 100000, 128, 64)
    nums = [
        _bounded_u32(rng, 1000),
        _bounded_u32(rng, 100000),
        _bounded_u32(rng, 128),
        _bounded_u32(rng, 64),
        _bounded_u32(rng, 3),
    ]
    for v in nums:
        out.append(_u32_le(v))
    # Emit a few floats
    for _ in range(3):
        out.append(_f32_le(_interesting_float(rng)))

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    chunks: List[bytes] = []

    # Magic header to make the buffer recognizable and stable
    chunks.append(b'FAISS\x00BUF\x01')

    # Emit several cycles corresponding to potential consumption order in stubs
    # Each cycle: [string][u32 numbers][float][string] ... to give variety
    cycles = rng.randint(3, 8)
    for _ in range(cycles):
        _emit_string_block(rng, chunks, 'key', min_len=1, max_len=24)
        _emit_numbers_block(rng, chunks)
        _emit_string_block(rng, chunks, 'pname', min_len=3, max_len=20)
        _emit_numbers_block(rng, chunks)
        # Additional free-form payload for MatrixStats::do_comment %s
        payload_len = rng.randint(0, 24)
        payload = _rand_ascii(rng, payload_len if payload_len > 0 else 0, payload_len)
        chunks.append(_u32_le(len(payload)))
        chunks.append(payload)
        # Extra float dedicated to formatting with %.3f
        chunks.append(_f32_le(_interesting_float(rng)))

    # Trailing padding of random bytes to allow parsers reading beyond exact boundaries
    pad_len = rng.randint(8, 32)
    pad = bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(pad_len))
    chunks.append(pad)

    data = b''.join(chunks)
    # Ensure total size <= 4096
    return data[:4096]

import string
from typing import List

# Data type: filename for output
# The fuzz target expects a writable filesystem path. The harness provides a
# temp directory and will substitute FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME() with a path pointing
# to random fuzzable data. Our job is to provide a bytes buffer that the fuzzer
# will use as the content backing that filename string.
#
# Strategy:
# - Generate plausible POSIX-like paths with varying characteristics:
#   - Shallow/bare filenames
#   - Nested directories (the harness typically ensures parent dirs exist or
#     normalizes it to a temp dir). We keep it relative to avoid absolute paths
#     outside sandbox.
#   - Different extensions (".dat", ".txt", ".gnuplot", no extension)
#   - Include safe characters plus some edge cases (spaces, dashes, underscores)
#   - Limit size well under 4096 bytes.
# - Ensure the produced byte sequence is a valid UTF-8 C-string when read by
#   the fuzzer as filename content.
# - Avoid characters that are likely to be invalid in filenames on common
#   platforms (no NUL, no path traversal like ".." at start, no control chars).
#
# Notes:
# - The target APIs only use the path string to open/create the file and write
#   gnuplot-friendly data. They do not read from our buffer; only the path
#   matters being writable.
# - We keep paths relative and simple, e.g., "out/foo_123.gnuplot".

SAFE_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_ "
EXTENSIONS = ["", ".txt", ".dat", ".out", ".gnuplot", ".gp", ".csv"]
DIR_NAMES = [
    "out", "tmp", "results", "plots", "data", "gnp", "o", "p"
]


def _rand_filename(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Choose number of directories (0-3)
    depth = rng.choices([0, 1, 2, 3], weights=[4, 3, 2, 1])[0]
    parts: List[str] = []

    for _ in range(depth):
        base_len = rng.randint(1, 8)
        if rng.random() < 0.6:
            name = rng.choice(DIR_NAMES)
        else:
            name = ''.join(rng.choice(SAFE_CHARS) for _ in range(base_len)).strip()
            if not name:
                name = "d"
        parts.append(name)

    # File base name
    base_len = rng.randint(3, 16)
    base = ''.join(rng.choice(SAFE_CHARS) for _ in range(base_len)).strip()
    if not base:
        base = "f"

    # Sometimes add a numeric or timestamp-like suffix
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        base += f"_{rng.randint(0, 99999)}"
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        base += f"-{rng.randint(0, 23):02d}{rng.randint(0,59):02d}{rng.randint(0,59):02d}"

    ext = rng.choice(EXTENSIONS)

    parts.append(base + ext)

    path = "/".join(parts)

    # Avoid leading/trailing slashes and parent traversal
    path = path.lstrip("/")
    path = path.replace("..", "__")
    # Ensure non-empty
    if not path:
        path = "out.dat"

    # Optionally prepend a top-level folder
    if rng.random() < 0.6 and not path.startswith(("out/", "tmp/", "results/", "plots/")):
        path = rng.choice(["out", "tmp", "results", "plots"]) + "/" + path

    # Cap length
    return path[:200]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # With small probability, generate a very short name
    if rng.random() < 0.15:
        fname = rng.choice(["out.dat", "plot.gp", "a", "o.txt"])  # simple, valid
    else:
        fname = _rand_filename(rng)

    # Ensure it's valid UTF-8 and does not exceed 4096 bytes
    data = fname.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
    if len(data) == 0:
        data = b"out.dat"
    return data[:4096]
